title: PM chairs valedictory session of Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment
subtitle:
PM calls for a whole-of-nation approach for success of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan

PM calls for greater Jan Bhagidari in early identification of disabilities and overcoming social stigma
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 9:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the valedictory session of the Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan earlier today.
The Summit brought together Ministers and senior officials from States and Union Territories for focused deliberations on strengthening social inclusion, empowerment of people with disabilities, prevention of substance abuse and innovative approaches to public participation.
Prime Minister appreciated the extensive deliberations and observed that the discussions and action points emerging from the Summit reflected a shared sense of purpose among the Centre and States. He emphasised that the spirit of competitive and cooperative federalism should guide implementation, with States learning from one another’s experiences and innovations.
Emphasising the importance of Jan Bhagidari, Prime Minister observed that community participation could play a significant role in creating awareness among parents about developmental disabilities and the importance of early identification. He noted that hesitation, fear of social stigma and lack of awareness often prevent parents from recognising or seeking timely support for their children. He observed that a community-based approach could help address parental hesitation and make early intervention more acceptable. He called for innovative approaches to awareness generation, particularly by leveraging technology to communicate important messages in simple and accessible ways. He also suggested that States could organise start-up competitions to encourage young innovators to develop affordable aids and assistive devices, particularly for improving mobility, accessibility and participation in sports and everyday activities.
Discussing the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, Prime Minister emphasised that efforts to address substance abuse must go beyond routine and symbolic activities. He suggested involving schools through essay-writing, debates, oratory competitions and other activities to generate awareness among young people and encourage wider societal participation. He also highlighted the importance of sharing the experiences of individuals who have successfully overcome addiction.
Emphasising a whole-of-nation approach, Prime Minister called for greater involvement of communities, spiritual organisations, educational institutions and Ministries in efforts towards a Nasha Mukt Bharat. He stressed that lasting behavioural change could be achieved only when society itself became an active participant in the movement.
Prime Minister reiterated that the Centre and States are partners in a common national endeavour, and that the collective commitment demonstrated during the Summit should be carried forward in the spirit of competitive and cooperative federalism, contributing towards an inclusive and empowered Viksit Bharat.

title: PM to inaugurate First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum on 20 November
subtitle: Three-day Forum to bring together scholars, academics, experts and cultural representatives to explore the shared civilisational heritage of SCO countries
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum on 20 November 2026 at around 5:30 PM at Purana Qila, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
Being held from 20 to 22 November 2026, the Forum aims to celebrate the rich and interconnected civilisational heritage of the region, strengthen people-to-people ties and promote cross-cultural dialogue and cooperation.
The initiative builds upon the proposal made by the Prime Minister at the SCO Summit in Tianjin, China in 2025 to establish a dedicated platform for civilisational dialogue under the SCO framework. The proposal was subsequently welcomed in the Bishkek Declaration of SCO.
The inaugural ceremony will feature “Civilisations in Conversation - Cultural Show”, a presentation combining music, dance, visual storytelling and narration. Based on the theme “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam - The World Is One Family”, it will highlight cultural connections across India and Eurasia.
The Forum will also feature exhibitions showcasing India's archaeological, artistic and literary heritage titled “ASTITVA – The Essence of Our Existence.” It will offer an immersive account of Delhi's history through archaeological evidence dating from 1200 BCE to 1200 CE, including excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries. The “Mahabharat Scroll Pavilion - Anant: A Rare 18th Century Mahabharata Scroll” will showcase an illustrated scroll reflecting India's rich epic and artistic traditions.
Four thematic sessions will be held on 21 and 22 November, bringing together scholars, academics, subject experts and cultural representatives. Discussions will cover cultural expressions such as music and performing arts, textiles, cuisine, traditional games; shared traditions in art and architecture; language and literary traditions, including scripts and manuscripts; and monastic trails and philosophical traditions.

title: English rendering of PM’s address during inauguration of FICCI Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention in Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 1:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Namaskar. FICCI President Brother Anant Goenka ji, members of FICCI, industry leaders, innovators, ladies and gentlemen.
On several occasions in the past, I have had the opportunity to attend and be a part of programmes associated with FICCI. But today’s occasion is somewhat special. FICCI is completing 100 years since its establishment. For an institution to remain alert and active continuously for 100 years, to keep moving forward with changing times, and to continue playing an active role in the country’s economic journey, is a very significant achievement. On this occasion, I wholeheartedly congratulate all those who have been associated with this institution, both in the past and the present, and extend my very best wishes to all of you.
Friends,
Over the past 100 years, India’s economy has seen many phases. We witnessed the License-Permit-Quota Raj, we saw the unsuccessful experiment of nationalisation, and then in the 21st century came a time when India’s economy began to be counted among the “Fragile Five.”
But during the past 12 years, the people of India, all of you, have worked very hard. Our youth, our farmers, our worker brothers and sisters, and all of you from the industry world have changed this situation. Today, India has the fastest pace of growth, and at the same time the pace at which people are coming out of poverty is also unprecedented.
Friends,
The latest World Bank report is something that fills all of us with pride. The report says that in just 12–13 years, 50 crore Indians have defeated poverty.
Friends,
When the slogan “Garibi Hatao” was given in the 1970s, the country's population itself was around 50 crore. Poverty could have been removed even then. But FICCI is also a witness to the fact that there were shortcomings in policies at that time, and unfortunately there were shortcomings in intent as well. I will not go into detail on that.
But friends,
FICCI is also a witness to the fact that when work was carried out with the right policies and when the government moved forward with the right intent, then within just 12–13 years, 50 crore poor people emerged from poverty. And this shows that the level at which India is moving today, the path on which India is progressing today, is the right one, is precise, and guarantees the nation's success.
Friends,
Today, India is the fastest-growing major economy in the world. Estimates by major institutions suggest that India will continue to grow at a rate of around 7 percent. One more figure attracted everyone's attention in October. In the month of October, India’s goods exports reached nearly 50 billion dollars. And this is India’s highest-ever monthly goods export figure. I am singing your praises here, and you are sitting quietly! Such is India’s performance that Moody’s Ratings, S&P Global Ratings, Fitch Ratings, the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank, every such agency is revising our growth projections upward.
Friends,
Our scriptures gave us a very important message thousands of years ago: “Uddharet Atmana Atmanam Na Atmanam Avasadayet.” That is, we must uplift ourselves, recognise our own capabilities, learn from our shortcomings, and continuously strive to become better. The next leap begins with honest self-reflection. To move forward, it is necessary that we engage in self-reflection from time to time. And this applies not only to individuals, but also to industry and to the nation. During its 100-year journey, FICCI has witnessed Indian industry achieve a great deal. Now the time has come to determine what Indian industry can achieve over the next 20 years. How can you increase your contribution to the journey of a Developed India and an Atmanirbhar Bharat? It may be very easy to continue working in businesses where you are already established, and they may offer short-term benefits as well. But industry must also prepare for the demands that will emerge in the future at both the national and global levels. We must work on those capabilities that, in this era of the weaponisation of resources, become all of our responsibility to secure the nation's future. Therefore, my request to you is this: in every long-term investment decision over the next 20 years, make India First your foundation. This will make the country self-reliant and will also open new opportunities for the growth of your businesses.
Friends,
You just showed a documentary. Now you must decide whether it should make us hold our heads high or bow them low. I know you will not clap right now. Think about it. One hundred years have passed, but in 1930 Gandhiji came to you and said the same thing, and after so many years I am still having to say the same thing. Is this your success or your failure? Do not listen to me, at least listen to Gandhi. He too spoke about Swadeshi. He too spoke about what we today call Atmanirbhar Bharat. Yet you have completed 100 years and things remain where they were. Therefore, I say that in the documentary you have made, add these two sentences of mine and take it to every household.
Friends,
Let me give you the example of the pharmaceutical industry. Everyone is sitting here and knows this. India is known as the Pharmacy of the World. Yet despite this, India imports APIs, bulk drugs, and drug intermediates worth billions of dollars every year. There are hundreds of such categories where we still depend on imports. Our pharmaceutical industry must understand which ingredients can be produced within India. In which sectors can we invest in new technologies and large production plants so that we become competitive with other countries? We already have strength in finished medicines. Now we must also build capability in ingredients.
Friends,
There are similar challenges in iron and steel. India exports iron ore worth thousands of crores of rupees, yet we also import finished steel. Our industry must think about which grades of steel we are importing, so that we can develop the technology to manufacture them ourselves. Similar opportunities exist in aluminium. India possesses huge reserves of bauxite measured in thousands of tonnes. Yet we import specialised aluminium alloys and other products. We must develop the capability to manufacture these products domestically. We also need expertise in the minerals value chain so that greater value addition takes place within India. Tell me, what kind of country is it where wheat is exported and bread is imported? Ask yourselves that question.
Friends,
Let me give you another figure. India is such a large country, yet our share in global agricultural exports is only around two to two-and-a-half percent. Our corporate world is afraid of investing in agriculture and tends to stay away from it.
Friends,
We must change this situation together. It should be viewed as a major opportunity linked to value addition and the food-processing industry. In the last 12 years, the share of processed food in agri-food exports has increased from 13 percent to more than 20 percent. It is necessary that industry comes together today and creates a strategy and a complete plan for the future, identifying what we are producing and what the world needs. I urge our industries to increase their investments in India’s agriculture sector. Create dependable procurement systems keeping specific overseas markets in mind, and develop products that are in demand there. This will enable Indian products to become India's identity in global markets.
Friends,
Just as in these sectors, India has enormous opportunities in daily engineering products as well. India’s share in global exports of hand tools and power tools is still quite small. We can work in this sector to increase our presence in the global market. Our large companies can help smaller companies develop manufacturing capacities of the necessary quality and scale. Machinery manufacturing is another sector waiting for us. A great deal can be done there. Together, we can manufacture machinery needed by developing countries, especially those in the Global South. Our industry can explore markets for packaging equipment, irrigation systems, and factory-related machinery, and can evaluate what more can be done in these sectors.
Friends,
No country progresses without respecting its farmers, its small entrepreneurs, its industries, its wealth creators, and its taxpayers. A nation does not progress by insulting them day and night. Some of you may know this, perhaps Pankaj bhai knows it. Once there was a major gathering of the Income Tax Department in Gujarat. I had only recently become Chief Minister then and did not know much about governance. This must have been around 2001–02, about 25 years ago. All the major Income Tax officers were present. I told them, “When will you stop treating everyone like a thief? What kind of approach is that?” They too work for the nation. Are we alone responsible for serving the country? Every citizen serves the nation. Everyone deserves respect. If I speak of industry, in recent years the government's focus has been strongly on Ease of Doing Business. In 2014, the basic corporate tax rate was 30 percent. We reduced it to 22 percent. Today, there is no income tax on earnings up to ₹12 lakh in India. I know you will not clap, because however much one gives, your appetite never seems to be satisfied. I have exempted income up to ₹12 lakh from tax. Did you increase the salaries of your employees? Did you increase the number of employees? No. The attitude remains: “Modi ji, you do it, we will see.”
But friends,
It took courage to provide such a major income tax relief. This has greatly increased people's purchasing power. We simplified the systems of returns and refunds, so that taxpayers' money does not remain unnecessarily stuck in the system. Earlier, refunds would take eight months. Today, refunds arrive within a week. Do they arrive or not? Then at least clap! Because I am unable to understand whether what we are doing is useful to you or whether we are doing it for no reason. Due to GST reforms, taxes on many products have come down. This has increased demand and directly benefited our industries and business houses.
Friends,
Over the past few years, India has entered into trade agreements with many countries around the world. Have the people of FICCI ever sat down and thought about this? When free trade agreements are signed with major economies of the world, it means doors have opened for you. Have you made any plans to seize those opportunities, or will I have to come here and explain that as well?
Friends, I speak honestly.
There cannot be a greater historic opportunity than this. If you do not benefit from all these efforts of mine, then who will? Please tell me that. I am doing this for you, and through you, for the nation. You are a very important medium. Recognise your strength. We have a domestic market of 140 crore people, and sometimes I feel that this itself has become your problem. Because you know that whatever you manufacture, someone will buy it. If one person in a big city does not buy it, someone in a smaller city will. If not there, then someone in a large village. If not there, then someone in a small village. “My product will sell anyway.” This mindset cannot continue. Times have changed. You will have to improve quality. Do not consider 140 crore Indians merely as an assured market. And sometimes, forgive me, I feel embarrassed. Today I am speaking openly with you. There are two kinds of people. I do not know whether both groups are present here. One group consists of builders and property developers. They construct a large tower and then hold back one or two units. They tell buyers, “This one is for me” or “This one is for my son,” but if you really want it, perhaps we can sell it. The customer immediately thinks that must be the highest-quality unit. Then there is another group, which I suspect is more common here. They tell customers, “This is export quality!” What do you think of the people of this country? Are they not entitled to quality products? Even today, you feel the need to tell them, “This is export quality.” And the customer thinks, “If it is for foreigners, then it must be good.” This mindset must change. My fellow countrymen deserve quality. Gopal, please explain this properly to everyone afterwards. But now the need is to make full use of the opportunities emerging in other countries as well. As the country moves forward on the Reform Express, the government too is ready to move in step with you.
And friends,
Today I want to speak openly. I have not come here merely for formality. I have come to meet you wholeheartedly. And I have come because I respect you. But your experience with previous governments has been so bitter that I am paying the price for it. This is not that old government. This is a friendly government. And this government knows how to maintain friendships. Since you are my true friends, I want you to do one thing. Will you do it? Will you? Without hesitation and without inhibition, write to me openly and tell me what reforms are still needed. I will keep asking you repeatedly to send suggestions openly. Even if I am able to act on only two out of a hundred suggestions, that will be my shortcoming. But do not hold back. The doors of the government, and the mind of the government, are completely open. I repeat, our domestic market should not become our comfort zone. We must come out of the psychology that our products will sell anyway because there are 140 crore customers. We should instead draw confidence from this market to compete in global markets. We must build that mindset. Invest in understanding the needs of customers across different regions of the world. Send teams. Conduct mapping studies. Understand who needs what and how it can be delivered. Develop user-friendly products. Create products in colours and designs preferred by local consumers. Otherwise, we all know how markets around the world are captured. Today, we cannot even be sure whether the Ganesh idols we worship were made in India or elsewhere.
Friends,
It is essential for us to invest in meeting global standards and building distribution networks that serve global needs. Our products should be such that they earn the confidence of customers in global markets and connect them with India. With this appeal, friends, today I have spoken very openly. I have shared my thoughts openly with all of you. I hope that your journey of 100 years has given you a great deal. But do not wait for another 100 years. Think about what you can give to the country in the next 10 years. If an organisation born in 1927 could see the country achieve independence within 20 years, then by the time India completes 100 years of independence, within 20 years we must certainly build a Developed India. We should move forward with that resolve.
And friends,
Independence was not just a slogan. Independence was a commitment. In the same way, a Developed India is not a slogan; it is a commitment. This commitment must be lived by all 140 crore Indians. And if we live it, we will achieve victory. With this spirit, I extend my very best wishes to all of you.
Thank you very much.
DISCLAIMER:
This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister’s address. Original address was delivered in Hindi.

subtitle:
STRONGER INDUSTRY–ACADEMIA PARTNERSHIPS ESSENTIAL TO ADVANCE RESEARCH, INNOVATION AND GLOBAL COMPETITIVENESS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS FOR CLOSER INDIA–US COLLABORATION IN TECHNOLOGY, CLEAN ENERGY AND EMERGING SECTORS

INDIA’S YOUNG TALENT, STARTUPS AND MSMEs OFFER IMMENSE OPPORTUNITIES FOR INVESTMENT AND PARTNERSHIP: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES THE 23RD INDO-US ECONOMIC SUMMIT 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasised that the shared democratic values of India and the United States provide a strong foundation for expanding bilateral trade, investment and technological cooperation. He observed that democratic institutions, stable policies, an independent judiciary and sustained engagement with stakeholders strengthen investor confidence and create opportunities for economic growth.
Shri Birla made these observations while addressing the 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit 2026. Describing India and the United States as two of the world's largest democracies, he said that strong and vibrant democratic institutions contribute to stable and responsive policymaking. Democracy provides space for diverse voices and ensures that the views of industry, trade, agriculture, technology, students and other stakeholders are taken into account while framing policies and laws, he added. He highlighted individual liberty, freedom of expression, equality before the law and an independent judiciary as important pillars of India's democratic framework. A stable policy environment, predictable taxation policies and regular engagement between industry and policymakers, he noted, encourage investment and strengthen economic partnerships.
Shri Birla appreciated the contribution of the Indo-American Chamber of Commerce in promoting economic engagement between the two countries since its establishment in 1968. He commended its successive leadership for facilitating dialogue, expanding trade relations, encouraging technology partnerships and creating employment opportunities. India's growing pool of skilled human resources, he said, offers considerable scope for further strengthening these partnerships.
Calling for closer collaboration between industry and academic institutions, Shri Birla urged businesses to work with universities, IITs, IIITs, engineering colleges and other technical institutions to advance research and innovation. He noted that investment by industry in research has played a significant role in driving technological progress across the world. Stronger partnerships between industry and educational institutions, he said, would help India develop new technologies, enhance competitiveness and establish leadership in emerging sectors.
Referring to the pharmaceutical sector, Shri Birla noted that Indian medicines enjoy wide international recognition, particularly in African countries. He emphasised the need for pharmaceutical companies and universities to undertake joint research to address emerging healthcare needs. Advances in AI and medical technology, he said, offer significant opportunities for innovation. He also highlighted India's progress towards self-reliance in defence under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, as well as its growing capabilities in defence manufacturing and exports.
Describing India's young population as a major strength, Shri Birla said that the ideas, skills and innovative capabilities of young Indians are contributing significantly to the country's development. He noted that India's expanding startup ecosystem has produced solutions to several global challenges. Micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), too, offer substantial opportunities for investment, technological cooperation and employment generation. He encouraged businesses from India and the United States to forge partnerships that leverage their respective strengths and expand opportunities in international markets.
On energy cooperation, Shri Birla observed that industrial growth, the expansion of data centres and investments in technology are driving an increase in energy demand. He stressed that industrial development must go hand in hand with environmental responsibility and highlighted India's efforts to promote clean and green energy. Greater collaboration among industry, scientists and researchers, he said, could accelerate innovation in energy technologies and support sustainable economic growth.
Shri Birla noted that developments in one country increasingly affect economies and societies across the world. Emphasising the importance of peace, stability and mutual trust, he said that India has consistently advocated collective efforts to address global challenges. Guided by the philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, India believes that countries must work together in a spirit of mutual respect to advance economic progress and social well-being.
Shri Birla expressed confidence that deliberations during the summit would generate fresh ideas for cooperation in industry, trade, technology, research and innovation. He emphasised that economic development must be inclusive, ensure equal opportunities and contribute to social welfare. Shared prosperity and human well-being, he said, must remain the guiding objectives of international cooperation.
नई दिल्ली में आयोजित 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit के उद्घाटन सत्र को संबोधित किया।

भारत की विशाल आर्थिक संभावनाएँ, कुशल मानव संसाधन और विनिर्माण क्षमता तथा अमेरिका की उन्नत तकनीक एवं अनुसंधान क्षमता मिलकर भविष्य की तकनीकों के संयुक्त विकास के नए अवसर खोल सकती हैं। AI, Semiconductors, Space Technology और Digital Infrastructure के साथ MSMEs, Startups, Women-led Entrepreneurship और Skill Development में सहयोग को बढ़ावा देना आवश्यक है। NISAR उपग्रह मिशन और अंतरिक्ष सहयोग इस साझेदारी की वैज्ञानिक क्षमता के उदाहरण हैं। भारत में निवेश केवल एक उभरते बाजार में भागीदारी नहीं, बल्कि विश्व की सबसे महत्वपूर्ण विकास संभावनाओं से जुड़ने का अवसर है।

title: CCRH Organises National Campaign on Antimicrobial Resistance to Promote Responsible Antimicrobial Use
subtitle:
Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Calls for Collective Action, Greater Public Awareness and Stronger Research to Combat AMR

CCRH Launches Dedicated AMR Webpage and Releases Bilingual Awareness Booklet
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 3:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy (CCRH), under the Ministry of Ayush, organised a National Campaign on Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) in New Delhi today to promote responsible antimicrobial use, strengthen public awareness, and highlight the importance of scientific research and coordinated action. The campaign was organised under the theme “One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now” with the tagline “Act Together. Fight AMR. Protect the Future.”
Addressing the gathering, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, emphasised that antibiotics should not be used indiscriminately and are not required for every illness. He noted that antibiotics are ineffective against viral infections such as the common cold and flu. However, self-medication, use of leftover medicines and consumption of antibiotics without medical advice contribute to the growing challenge of AMR.
Referring to the message of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during his Mann Ki Baat address on 28 December 2025, Shri Prataprao Jadhav reiterated: “Do not take antibiotics without a doctor's advice.” He underscored that public awareness and collective responsibility are essential to promoting the judicious use of medicines.
Highlighting four key priorities to address AMR, Shri Jadhav called for the judicious use of antibiotics strictly on medical prescription and completion of the prescribed course; strengthening infection prevention through clean drinking water, hand hygiene, sanitation, food safety and vaccination; enhancing research, laboratory infrastructure and surveillance systems; and integrating AMR and rational medicine use into medical education and the training of healthcare professionals.
Ms. Alarmelmangai D., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, delivered the special address, highlighting the potential of the Ministry of Ayush to contribute significantly through its research institutions, clinical networks and academic activities. Appreciating CCRH’s initiative, she noted that the Council has taken steps to transform AMR awareness activities from annual observances into a sustained, structured and comprehensive national campaign.
Dr. Subhash Kaushik, Director General, CCRH, outlined the Council's initiatives and research perspectives on AMR. He highlighted ongoing efforts in research, awareness generation, capacity building and institutional collaboration to strengthen scientific understanding and stakeholder engagement.
Dr. Preetha Kizhakkuttil, Advisor (Homoeopathy), Ministry of Ayush; Dr. Tarkeshwar Jain, Chairperson, National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH); and Dr. K. C. Muraleedharan, Deputy Director General, CCRH, were also present on the occasion, along with senior officials from the Ministry of Ayush, NCH and CCRH.
A key highlight of the programme was the launch of a dedicated CCRH webpage on Antimicrobial Resistance and the release of a bilingual AMR Awareness Booklet. These initiatives aim to improve access to reliable information, enhance public understanding and encourage responsible antimicrobial practices.
The programme also featured the administration of an AMR Pledge, reaffirming the collective commitment to responsible antimicrobial use and efforts to prevent and contain antimicrobial resistance.
Antimicrobial resistance occurs when microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites, develop resistance to medicines designed to combat them, making infections increasingly difficult to treat. AMR poses a significant public health challenge and requires coordinated action across human health, animal health, agriculture and environmental sectors under the One Health approach.
The campaign underscores the Ministry of Ayush and CCRH's commitment to strengthening research, expanding public awareness and promoting responsible antimicrobial practices through coordinated stakeholder engagement to address the growing challenge of AMR.

The 14th Indian Fisheries and Aquaculture Forum (14IFAF), a major international scientific conference in fisheries and aquaculture, commenced today at the ICAR–Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (ICAR-CIFA), in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The three-day conference, being held from 18th to 20th November, 2026, is jointly organised by the Asian Fisheries Society, Indian Branch (AFSIB), ICAR-CIFA, Department of Fisheries, Government of India, National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), Fisheries and Animal Resources Development (FARD) Department, Government of Odisha, and the Association of Aquaculturists.
The conference is being held under the theme
“Transforming Aquaculture and Fisheries: Bridging Science and Society”,
with a focus on advancing scientific knowledge, promoting technological innovations and strengthening collaboration among researchers, policymakers, industry stakeholders and farming communities.
The conference was inaugurated by Dr Eduardo Leano, Director General, Network of Aquaculture Centres in Asia-Pacific (NACA), Bangkok. In his inaugural address, he emphasised the need to accelerate innovation and technology adoption to transform the aquaculture sector.
Dr J. K. Jena, Deputy Director General (Fisheries Science), ICAR, highlighted the importance of greater investment in frontier research and the development of robust value chains. Dr B. K. Behera, Chief Executive, NFDB, stressed strengthening fisheries cooperatives to improve the livelihoods of fishers. Dr C. Vasudevappa, former Vice-Chancellor, NIFTEM, Kundli, Haryana, emphasised the importance of ensuring fish quality and enhancing consumer acceptance.
Other distinguished speakers included Dr A. E. Eknath, former Director General, NACA; Dr K. M. Rajesh, Secretary, AFSIB; Dr Dilip Kumar, former Director, ICAR-CIFE, Mumbai; and Dr I. Karunasagar, Advisor, FAO Reference Centre, NITTE University, Mangaluru. They shared their perspectives on emerging priorities, research advancements and future opportunities in fisheries and aquaculture.
Earlier, Dr P. K. Sahoo, Director, ICAR-CIFA and Convener of the Conference, welcomed the dignitaries and delegates. He highlighted the importance of strengthening science–industry–farmer linkages, promoting international cooperation and translating research outcomes into practical solutions for the farming community. He informed that the forum has attracted over 1,000 participants from India and six other countries, comprising scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, entrepreneurs, industry representatives and farmers.
Key areas of deliberation during the three-day conference include sustainable fisheries management, aquatic ecosystem conservation, artificial intelligence (AI), genome editing, precision aquaculture, advanced breeding technologies, feed development, aquatic animal health and genetic improvement.
A concurrent exhibition featuring 20 agencies is showcasing technologies, innovations, products and services in fisheries and aquaculture. The exhibition provides an opportunity for industry stakeholders, researchers and farmers to interact, explore technological solutions and establish collaborative partnerships. The inaugural ceremony also featured the release of scientific publications and presentation of the Fellow Awards of the Association of Aquaculturists to eminent fisheries scientists in recognition of their contributions to the sector.
The three-day forum aims to facilitate scientific exchange, foster national and international cooperation and identify actionable strategies for sustainable, inclusive and technology-driven growth of India's fisheries and aquaculture sector.

title: India’s Scale, Talent and Manufacturing Strength Complement US Capital, Technology and Innovation: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal
subtitle:
India and US Natural Partners in Building Trusted and Resilient Supply Chains Amid Global Uncertainty: Shri Goyal at 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit

Growing Global Business Interest in India; India and Egypt to Explore Preferential or Free Trade Agreement to Boost Bilateral Trade and Investment: Shri Goyal

India and Italy Aim to Expand Bilateral Trade to €50 Billion Following Implementation of India-EU FTA: Shri Goyal

Shri Piyush Goyal Outlines Five-Point TRUST Agenda for Stronger India-US Partnership: Trusted Supply Chains, Raising Talent, Unlocking Bharat Beyond Metros, Speaking Candidly and Tracking Outcomes
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 9:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today, addressing the 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit organised by the Indo-American Chamber of Commerce (IACC) in New Delhi, highlighted the significance of the India-US economic partnership, stating that the United States brings capital, technology and innovation as the world's largest economy, while India offers scale, talent, manufacturing strength, competitiveness and a rapidly transforming economy.
Shri Goyal said that India's digital transformation was taking the country forward as the world's fastest-growing large economy towards the goal of Viksit Bharat, a developed and prosperous nation that provides a better life and future for 1.4 billion Indians.
Referring to the theme of this year's Summit, 'One Shared Future', Shri Goyal said that the partnership had progressed from 'Shaping a Shared Future', the theme of the previous year's Summit, to jointly owning and working towards that future. He expressed confidence that the shared future between India and the United States would become a defining feature for both countries and the world.
The Minister said that India and the United States are two vibrant democracies that shape the global narrative. Recalling Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's message while congratulating the United States on its Independence Day on 4th July, he said that the India-US partnership is a force for global good and should also become an engine for global growth. He congratulated the United States on celebrating 250 years of independence and extended his best wishes to the American people.
Emphasising that trust was the foundation of India's international partnerships, Shri Goyal said that India offers a trusted partnership and stands by its friends through difficult times. Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's observation that trust has become a fundamental question before the world, the Minister said that businesses were operating in an increasingly volatile and uncertain global environment, marked by two ongoing wars, the West Asia crisis and the Russia-Ukraine war.
He said that the world needed not merely supply chains but trusted supply chains, where partners shared a common vision, respected the rule of law and honoured contracts. India and the United States, he added, were natural partners in building such a chain of trust.
Highlighting recent developments in bilateral and multilateral engagement, Shri Goyal said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump had met at the Quad Leaders' Summit in Manila two days earlier. The two leaders had announced the first Quad Business Leaders Forum in early 2027. He expressed confidence that IACC and other organisations would play an important role in bringing together leading Indian businesses to represent the country at the Forum.
Sharing his recent interactions with businesses in the United States, the Minister said that during his visit to New York last month, he observed a growing interest among businesses in expanding their engagement with India. Companies were looking to establish Global Capability Centres, expand design and innovation operations, research and development activities, business processes and offices in India, recognising the country's large pool of skilled talent.
He said that similar enthusiasm for engagement with India was evident during his recent visits to Egypt and Italy. During discussions with Egyptian counterparts and the Prime Minister of Egypt, both sides had agreed to ask their officials to explore finalising the terms of reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or a Free Trade Agreement to expand trade and investment between the two countries.
During his joint business forum and joint business committee meetings with the Deputy Prime Minister of Italy, H.E. Mr. Antonio Tajani, Shri Goyal said that both sides had resolved to pursue ambitious trade targets. While the immediate objective was to increase bilateral trade to 20 billion euros by 2029, from the current level of 12 billion dollars, both countries had agreed that India and Italy had the potential to expand trade to 50 billion euros once the India-EU Free Trade Agreement comes into effect in the first quarter or first half of calendar year 2027. He said that businesses, importers and exporters should be encouraged to pursue more ambitious targets.
Highlighting India's export performance, Shri Goyal said that India had set an ambitious target of achieving $1 trillion in exports during the current year, registering nearly 16 per cent growth, and had already achieved $480 billion in exports during the first six months, from April to September. India's exports had reached an all-time record of $863 billion in the previous year, while October recorded the country's highest-ever monthly exports of goods and services at $90 billion.
The Minister said that when the Government engaged with industry and Export Promotion Councils earlier this year to determine the export target, India had the option of setting a modest target of 5 per cent growth, particularly when the International Monetary Fund had projected global trade growth of around 2 per cent during April-May. However, industry chambers and exporters demonstrated confidence, strength and resilience and collectively decided to aim for $1 trillion in exports, representing nearly 16 per cent growth. He emphasised that high ambitions and challenging targets were essential for achieving success.
Highlighting India's digital transformation, Shri Goyal said that a street vendor and a five-star hotel today both use digital payment systems such as the Unified Payments Interface (UPI). This had helped bridge the digital divide in the country. He also highlighted the role of the JAM trinity in delivering the Government's welfare measures, including payments, scholarships and pensions, directly into beneficiaries' bank accounts in a seamless and timely manner. By plugging leakages in the system, these initiatives had helped the Government save lakhs of crores of rupees, amounting to billions of dollars.
The Minister emphasised the need to extend the benefits of modern technology to entrepreneurs and businesses in every part of the country. Technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Computer-Aided Design and Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAD/CAM), machine learning and advanced manufacturing should reach the remotest corners of India.
He said that the benefits of global trade, international engagement and preferential, free trade and bilateral trade agreements must reach the smallest businesses and individuals. The benefits should extend to MSMEs, farmers, fishermen, Vishwakarmas, artisans, handicraft and handloom makers, as much as they do to large corporations.
In this context, Shri Goyal highlighted the Government's Export Promotion Mission, under which significant outreach efforts were being undertaken across every district of the country. The initiative aimed to encourage first-time exporters, enable them to access newer markets and support the export of newer products.
On technology cooperation, the Minister said that Artificial Intelligence and innovation were areas in which the United States had established considerable strengths, particularly in developing frontier models. India, too, was looking at the entire AI stack and would continue to focus on taking AI to 1.4 billion people. The IndiaAI Mission, AI Impact Summit, Semicon 2 and the growth of Global Capability Centres reflected India's engagement with emerging technologies.
He said that education and future skills would increasingly incorporate modern technologies. Healthcare and pharmaceuticals would also benefit from Artificial Intelligence and agents built on large language models, enabling smarter and more efficient delivery of healthcare and medicines. New discoveries would become more affordable, while biotechnology, medical devices and clinical research would be among the areas in which India would be at the forefront of global technological innovation and development.
Outlining five calls to action for strengthening the India-US economic partnership, Shri Goyal used the acronym TRUST to present his suggestions.
Under the first 'T', he called for transforming supply chains into resilient and trusted supply chains.
Under 'R', he called for raising talent together with friendly and partner countries. He reiterated his strong support for dual-degree programmes and stronger educational partnerships. Referring to Amity University and its leadership, he said that he had been keen to visit its large campus in the Netherlands but could not do so. He also highlighted the interest expressed by a large group in Egypt in connecting with Amity and other Indian universities to bring Indian education to Egypt, and urged the university to engage with them immediately.
The Minister said that India and the United States had built considerable talent partnerships through their universities over the years and that these relationships should be further strengthened. He said that he was working with some US universities to explore bringing them to India and invited American universities and students to consider India as part of their academic programmes.
He emphasised that global growth would increasingly be led by countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Exposure to Indian universities and colleges would help students from developed countries understand the culture and functioning of developing nations, enabling them to contribute more effectively to their own countries, economies, workplaces and businesses in the future.
Under 'U', Shri Goyal called for unlocking Bharat beyond the metropolitan cities, stressing that development should not remain confined to certain regions or urban centres. He recalled that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, upon assuming office in 2014, had emphasised equitable development across all parts of India, particularly eastern and northern India, which had not received their due share of development over the decades.
He said that the Government had focused on the development of the Northeastern states, resulting in significant progress in infrastructure, electricity, water supply, incubation centres and quality education, alongside efforts to bring industry to the region.
Similarly, the eastern belt, including Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh, had witnessed substantial transformation and development in recent years.
Under 'S', the Minister called for stakeholders to speak candidly with each other and flag the hurdles and difficulties they faced. He said that different arms of the Government were available to support businesses, address their concerns and help them expand their operations and reach global markets.
Under the final 'T', Shri Goyal called for tracking the outcomes of all initiatives and ensuring accountability for performance. He urged IACC to hold the Government accountable, monitor its work and ensure that the Government and industry continued to work together towards a better future and a stronger India-US partnership.
The Minister expressed appreciation for the work undertaken by IACC's regional chambers and extended his best wishes to the organisation, its regional chambers and members for continued success.

title: India and Indonesia Review Trade and Economic Cooperation at 2nd Working Group on Trade and Investment Meeting in New Delhi
subtitle: Indonesia is India’s Second-Largest Trading Partner in ASEAN, with Bilateral Trade of USD 24.78 Billion in FY 2025-26
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 9:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 2nd Meeting of the India-Indonesia Working Group on Trade and Investment (WGTI) was held at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi, in hybrid mode. The Indian delegation was led by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Shri Amit Verma, and the Indonesian delegation by Director of Bilateral Negotiation, Ministry of Trade, Indonesia, Ms Basaria Tiara Desika L. Gaol. Representatives of concerned Ministries, Departments and organisations of both countries also participated.
The meeting reviewed bilateral trade, which stood at USD 24.78 billion in FY 2025-26, with Indonesia accounting for 19.30 per cent of India’s trade with ASEAN. India underlined the importance of balanced and diversified trade and highlighted export opportunities in pharmaceuticals, vaccines and medical devices, automobiles and components, machinery, dairy, rice, spices, electronics, and solar and energy-related products.
The discussions focused on the resolution of issues faced by exporters, including market access for agricultural and animal products such as peanuts, horticultural products, buffalo meat and frozen shrimp, approval of establishments, halal certification, standards and certification requirements for tyres and automobiles, registration of pharmaceuticals and AYUSH products, and local content requirements in electronics. India proposed designating contact points in the counterpart agencies for time-bound resolution of these issues. Issues raised by Indonesia, including market access for agricultural products and India’s Quality Control Orders, were also discussed.
Both sides explored cooperation in the services sector, including mutual recognition of professional qualifications, mobility of professionals, social security, digital services, health, education and tourism. India also underlined the importance of an early conclusion of the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) Review.
The meeting, the first since the inaugural WGTI in August 2021, was convened pursuant to the India-Indonesia Joint Statement issued during the State Visit of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to Indonesia (6-8 July 2026), in which the leaders called for convening the 2nd WGTI in 2026 and emphasised fully utilising and strengthening the bilateral economic mechanisms and working towards concrete and business-oriented outcomes.
The two sides also deliberated on customs cooperation; critical minerals and mining; local currency settlement, the linkage of India’s UPI with Indonesia’s QRIS, and banking and insurance; energy, including renewable energy, green hydrogen and biofuels; fertilisers; port and air connectivity; and the implementation of the agreements and MoUs signed during the July 2026 visit.
The meeting reaffirmed the commitment of both sides to strengthening the India-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. India proposed that the WGTI meet regularly to sustain the momentum. The next meeting of the WGTI will be held in Indonesia.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls on FICCI to Evolve into a Global Chamber and Strengthen India’s Global Economic Engagement
subtitle:
Shri Goyal Urges Indian Businesses to Utilise Opportunities Opened by Recent Free Trade Agreements

Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights India’s Transformation in Infrastructure, Digital Connectivity and Financial Inclusion

Shri Goyal Appreciates Indian Industry’s Efforts in Sustaining Export Growth Amid Global Uncertainties

Shri  Goyal Urges Indian Industries to Lead the Journey Towards Viksit Bharat 2047
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, addressed the valedictory session of the FICCI Annual General Meeting in New Delhi, calling upon FICCI to reinvent itself as a global chamber and play a greater role in connecting Indian businesses with international markets, technologies and opportunities as it enters its second century.
Shri Goyal recalled that FICCI took shape around 1926–27 on the advice of Mahatma Gandhi, with the objective of promoting Swadeshi, supporting the freedom struggle and encouraging Indian entrepreneurship. He congratulated FICCI on approaching its centenary and acknowledged the contributions of its past presidents and leadership in India's journey towards independence, self-reliance and industrial development.
Shri Goyal noted the expanding market access available to Indian businesses through recent Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and urged Indian businesses to utilise the opportunities opened by these agreements. He said that India's preferential access to global markets, representing around USD 10 trillion in GDP until a few years ago, has expanded by an additional USD 60 trillion over the last four-and-a-half years, taking the total to approximately USD 70 trillion. With ongoing bilateral and multilateral trade engagements across eight to nine geographies, this is expected to expand to around USD 85 trillion, representing nearly 76 per cent of global GDP, over the next year to year-and-a-half.
Building on the expanding global opportunities for Indian businesses, Shri Goyal said that FICCI's next century should be guided by a more ambitious global outlook, with a focus on taking Indian products and services to international markets and bringing the best of the world to India. He said that India seeks to share its growth and future with the rest of the world while bringing global opportunities and capabilities to the country.
The Minister said that FICCI can no longer remain only an Indian chamber and must develop a stronger global presence. He called upon the organisation to build international partnerships, facilitate technology transfers, promote Indian enterprises overseas and help attract global companies to India for manufacturing, investment and the establishment of Global Capability Centres (GCCs).
Referring to his recent visits to Egypt and Italy, Shri Goyal said that the growing interest of international partners in working with India reflects the country's increasing global standing. He noted that discussions have been initiated to explore a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement with Egypt, while the forthcoming India–EU FTA has generated considerable interest among Italian businesses. He said that the commitment of international businesses to work with India reflects the growing opportunities for trade, investment and industrial cooperation.
Highlighting India's growing economic strength and global engagement, Shri Goyal said that India has set an ambitious target of achieving USD 1 trillion in exports in FY 2026–27. He noted that India recorded exports of USD 480 billion in the first six months of the current financial year, achieving 48 per cent of the annual target and registering growth of approximately 17 per cent. He also noted the record monthly exports of around USD 90 billion achieved in October, appreciating the contribution of Indian businesses in achieving this performance despite global uncertainties and geopolitical ch
allenges.
The Minister said that India's ambition to achieve USD 1 trillion in exports reflects the collective commitment of the Government and industry. Recalling discussions with Export Promotion Councils and industry associations earlier in the year, he said that the target was set despite projections of subdued global trade growth. He appreciated the efforts of Indian businesses in sustaining export growth amid ongoing global conflicts and disruptions.
The Minister spoke about India's transformation over the past decade, noting improvements in infrastructure, digital connectivity, financial inclusion and the banking sector. He said that India's strong macroeconomic fundamentals, skilled workforce, entrepreneurial ecosystem and decisive leadership have strengthened the country's ability to engage with the world from a position of strength and confidence.
Shri Goyal also underscored India's growing economic capabilities, noting that the country has emerged as the world's fastest-growing large economy. He referred to the significant reduction in non-performing loans in the banking sector, improved access to affordable credit and the expansion of financial inclusion. He highlighted that 56 crore Mudra loans have been supported by the Government, with more than 55 per cent extended to women entrepreneurs, enabling them to participate in the formal economy and pursue their entrepreneurial journeys.
Shri Goyal said that India's growing middle class, purchasing power and expanding domestic market provide a strong foundation for economic growth. He also referred to initiatives such as Make in India and Digital India, the provision of 12 crore toilets in rural households and the continued provision of free foodgrains to 80 crore people as part of the country's broader development journey.
Shri Goyal also drew attention towards the role of entrepreneurship in India's growt. Shri Goyal said that India's start-up ecosystem makes the country proud. Referring to his recent interaction with Indian start-ups in Italy, he noted the participation of entrepreneurs from cities such as Bikaner, Kota and Jamshedpur, who engaged with their Italian counterparts and explored potential business and investment opportunities.
The Minister said that the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat builds upon the spirit of Swadeshi that inspired the establishment of FICCI nearly a century ago. Referring to Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya’s philosophy, the Union Minister underscored its continued relevance and emphasised that self-reliance and the spirit of Swadeshi should remain the foundation of India’s economic development. He said that India must now move a step further by creating capabilities and strategic strengths that make the world increasingly dependent on Indian products, services, technologies and talent.
The Minister also highlighted India's growing capabilities in innovation and technology, referring to the achievements of Indian start-ups and the private space sector. He cited the successful launch of a rocket into space by an Indian private sector company in its first attempt, describing it as an important milestone for India's entrepreneurial and technological ecosystem. He also referred to international collaborations in the creative and technology sectors, observing that India is increasingly contributing to global innovation.
Shri Goyal urged FICCI to use its second century to take Indian industry to the world, support young entrepreneurs in future technologies, promote India as a destination for global manufacturing and investment, and extend technology to the remotest parts of the country, including farms, MSMEs and artisan communities. He emphasised that FICCI can play an important role as a bridge between India's 140 crore people and global markets and opportunities.
Concluding his address, Shri Piyush Goyal expressed confidence in India's ability to navigate the challenges of a turbulent global environment and emerge as a beacon of opportunity and growth. He called upon FICCI's leadership and members to persevere in their efforts and contribute to the country's journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Co-Chairs 23rd Session of India–Italy Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation in Rome
subtitle:
Shri Piyush Goyal addresses India–Italy Business and Innovation Forum; around 80 Indian business delegates, including 12 startups, participate

Both sides reaffirm shared target of €20 billion in bilateral trade by 2029

Discussions focus on expanding trade, investment and industrial cooperation
date:

content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal co-chaired the 23rd Session of the India–Italy Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation (JCEC) with H.E. Mr. Antonio Tajani, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Italy, in Rome on 18 November 2026. The Ministers reviewed the progress of bilateral economic and commercial cooperation and discussed measures to expand trade, investment and industrial partnerships. They reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the India–Italy Special Strategic Partnership, building on the Joint Strategic Action Plan 2025–2029 and the outcomes of the visit of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to Italy in May 2026.
The discussions covered cooperation in automotive and aerospace, Industry 4.0, agriculture and agri-technology, connectivity and energy, critical minerals, science and innovation, culture and tourism, skills development and entrepreneurship. Both sides highlighted the complementarities between India's growing manufacturing capabilities and skilled workforce and Italy's strengths in advanced manufacturing, engineering, machinery and technology. They encouraged greater industry participation, joint ventures, technology partnerships and integration into global value chains.
The Ministers also welcomed the successful conclusion of negotiations on the India–EU Free Trade Agreement and discussed its potential to expand market access, increase trade and investment flows and strengthen supply chains. In this context, they reaffirmed the shared target of achieving €20 billion in bilateral trade by 2029 and emphasised the need to diversify trade and scale up investments.
During his visit, Shri Piyush Goyal also held one-to-one meetings with CEOs and senior leaders of leading Italian companies, including Walter Tosto S.p.A., Nordimpianti System, Atitech, Magaldi Group and Bracco Group, on 17 November 2026. The discussions focused on investment, manufacturing and technology partnership opportunities in India.
The Minister also addressed the India–Italy Business and Innovation Forum in Rome, which brought together senior government leaders, industry associations and Italian companies, along with around 80 Indian business delegates, including 12 startups. Ahead of the Forum, Shri Goyal interacted with the Indian business delegation on opportunities for Indian businesses in Italy and the wider European market, including those arising from the India–EU Free Trade Agreement.
Three sectoral roundtables were organised as part of the Forum to explore opportunities arising from the complementary strengths of the two economies. The pharmaceuticals and chemicals roundtable identified partnership opportunities in pharmaceutical manufacturing, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), specialty chemicals, biotechnology and joint research and development. The industrial machinery and agri-food roundtable highlighted opportunities in automation, technology transfer, food-processing machinery, cold-chain infrastructure and packaging, aimed at reducing post-harvest losses and enhancing value addition. The automotive roundtable explored collaboration in electric and next-generation mobility, components, research and innovation, and sustainable manufacturing. Across the roundtables, participants emphasised joint ventures, investment partnerships and technology sharing as key means of translating discussions into tangible business outcomes.
The Innovation Forum was opened by Mr. Mauro Battocchi, Director General for Growth and Export Promotion, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Italy, and Ms. Vani Rao, Ambassador of India to Italy. Shri Piyush Goyal participated throughout the Forum and interacted with Indian and Italian delegates, encouraging both sides to explore avenues for collaboration and synergy in areas such as sustainability and technology and to build on the complementary strengths of the two innovation ecosystems.
At the Plenary Session, business associations presented the outcomes of the Business Forum, followed by addresses by H.E. Mr. Antonio Tajani and Shri Piyush Goyal. The sessions highlighted the strong complementarities between the two economies and underscored the shared commitment of India and Italy to deepen their economic partnership.
During his bilateral meeting with H.E. Mr. Antonio Tajani, the two Ministers reviewed the entire gamut of bilateral economic and commercial relations and discussed ways to further strengthen trade, investment and industrial cooperation. They reaffirmed their commitment to translating the vision of the two Prime Ministers into tangible outcomes through sustained engagement and closer business partnerships.
The visit provided fresh momentum to the India–Italy Special Strategic Partnership and reinforced the shared commitment to expanding bilateral trade, investment and business collaboration.

title: Telecom Manufacturing Zone, Gwalior Gains Momentum with Distribution of Letters of Intent to 25 Companies
subtitle:
Under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Leadership, India Moves from Telecom Services to Telecom Manufacturing: Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia

Initiative to strengthen India's domestic telecom manufacturing ecosystem, attract investment and generate employment opportunities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Madhya Pradesh, organised a Letter of Intent (LoI) Distribution Ceremony for 25 companies investing in the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), Gwalior, in Bhopal today. The event marked an important milestone in advancing India's vision of becoming a global hub for telecom manufacturing, innovation and technology development.
The ceremony was graced by Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav and Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia. Senior officials of the Government of India and the Government of Madhya Pradesh, along with representatives from the telecom and electronics industries, participated in the programme. The programme also marked the announcement of Phase-II of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone, signalling a significant step towards expanding the zone's manufacturing ecosystem and strengthening investment opportunities in the telecom and electronics sectors.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said
“
India has established itself as a global leader in telecom services. However, the time has now come for the next paradigm shift in the telecom industry. We must move from being a services nation to becoming a product nation. It is the responsibility of the Government of India to create an ecosystem that enables industry to establish manufacturing facilities and grow.
The Minister further emphasized, “Hon'ble Prime Minister's vision has always been that there was a time when India depended on the world, but today India is self-reliant. The day is not far when the world will depend on India. We must work towards making this vision a reality in the coming decade. This is India's time, and this is the time for Madhya Pradesh."
The Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav, highlighted “This is the first time in the history of India that we have been able to build a zone dedicated to telecom sector. It is the best example of how the Central and State Government work in tandem for rapid development of industry. For this zone, we have given approval to 170 acres of land through the Cabinet.”
The programme featured a presentation on the Telecom Manufacturing Zone project and its development roadmap by the Government of Madhya Pradesh. Industry representatives also shared their perspectives on investment opportunities and industry participation.
The Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior is envisaged as an integrated industrial cluster dedicated to telecom manufacturing, research and development, and innovation. Spread across approximately 170 acres, the zone will facilitate manufacturing activities in areas such as telecom equipment, components, optical fibre, software and passive infrastructure.
The latest engagement builds on the Department's continued efforts to attract investment through investor outreach programmes in New Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru. Earlier investor engagements in New Delhi and Mumbai had resulted in investment commitments of ₹5,500 crore, with a potential to generate nearly 20,000 employment opportunities.
The Telecom Manufacturing Zone is aligned with the vision of
Aatmanirbhar Bharat and “Make in India, Make for the World”
. It aims to strengthen domestic supply chains, reduce import dependence, encourage indigenous research and product development, enhance exports and position India as a trusted global destination for telecom manufacturing.
The distribution of Letters of Intent marks another significant step towards translating investor interest into manufacturing opportunities on the ground. The initiative reflects the strong partnership between the Central Government and the Government of Madhya Pradesh towards building a robust, globally competitive and self-reliant telecom manufacturing ecosystem.
The Telecom Manufacturing Zone, Gwalior, is poised to contribute to India's emergence as a global hub for telecom manufacturing, innovation and technological advancement.

title: Raksha Mantri and Japan’s Minister of Defense hold bilateral talks in Tokyo
subtitle: India & Japan agree to deepen defence cooperation across key domains and reaffirm commitment to peace & stability in Indo-Pacific
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 7:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh held a bilateral meeting with the Minister of Defense of Japan Mr Shinjiro Koizumi in Tokyo on November 19, 2026. The two Ministers welcomed the steady materialisation of India-Japan defence cooperation through close communication between them, including the holding of their third Defence Ministers’ Meeting within a short period of time, following their interactions in August and October this year.
Both the leaders welcomed the signing of LOI (Letter of Intent) toward the utilisation of firing ranges in India, whereby Japan Self-Defense Forces would, for the first time, conduct live-fire training etc., including those involving surface-to-ship missiles, at firing ranges in India. They concurred on accelerating coordination between the defence authorities of the two countries toward its early realisation.
The two Ministers welcomed the steady progress in materialising maritime security cooperation under the ‘Memorandum of Arrangement on Maritime Security Cooperation’ signed in August this year. In particular, they confirmed that the Working Group, headed at the JS/DG level, would follow up on working level talks on areas including enhancing mine counter-measures capabilities and exploring the possibility of joint development in naval shipbuilding and design.
The two Ministers agreed to further deepen cooperation towards creating an environment that would facilitate information sharing between the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force and the Indian Navy.
The two Ministers welcomed the deepening of cooperation through joint exercises between the respective Services, including the multilateral naval exercise ‘Malabar 2026’ involving Japan, the United States, India and Australia, and the Japan-India Maritime Exercise ‘JAIMEX26’, both conducted in Japan this month. They also concurred on further advancing exchanges between their respective Special Operations Forces.
Regarding defence equipment and technology cooperation, the two Ministers shared their expectation for an early conclusion of the UNICORN related arrangements, and the Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) by India by February 2027. They also affirmed that they would materialise defence R&D cooperation between DRDO and ATLA in the field of state-of-the-art missile and defence technologies.
The two Ministers concurred on promoting cooperation between the two air services in the field of Air Domain Awareness and confirmed that the working level talks would also be followed through the Working Group, headed at the JS/DG level.
Amid an increasingly complex and uncertain security environment in the Indo-Pacific region, the two Ministers concurred on further promoting multilateral defence cooperation, including trilateral cooperation, in addition to bilateral defence cooperation between Japan and India, and on advancing practical cooperation for peace and stability in the region.
The two Ministers shared their determination to steadily implement these concrete areas of cooperation and elevate Japan-India defence cooperation to greater heights, thereby contributing together to the peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific.
