title: Joint Statement : Fourth India-Japan 2+2 Foreign and Defence Ministerial Meeting
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 5:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh, Minister of External Affairs Dr S Jaishankar, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan Mr Motegi Toshimitsu and Minister of Defence of Japan Mr Koizumi Shinjiro held the fourth India-Japan 2+2 Foreign and Defence Ministerial Meeting in Tokyo on November 19, 2026.
The Ministers underscored the growing strategic convergence and trust between the two countries in an increasingly complex and uncertain international environment and stressed the importance of closer coordination under the India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership in addressing present geopolitical, economic and security challenges. As leading democracies and major economies of the world, the Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining and strengthening an international order which is free, open and based on the rule of law, respect for principles of national sovereignty and territorial integrity, and peaceful resolution of disputes without resorting to threat or use of force. They underlined the need for all countries to refrain from any attempt to unilaterally change the status quo.
The Ministers appreciated and committed to enhancing the synergy between the Indo-Pacific Oceans’ Initiative (IPOI) & Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions (MAHASAGAR) and the updated “Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP)” that contributes to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific.
The Ministers noted with satisfaction the significant development of bilateral cooperation since the last 2+2 Meeting in 2024. They welcomed the outcomes of the 15th and 16th India-Japan Annual Summits held in August 2025 and July 2026 respectively that provided leader-level strategic direction to deepening defence and security cooperation, economic partnership including economic security, energy resilience, technology, and innovation as well as people-to-people exchanges in developing a mutually complementary relationship. In advancing bilateral cooperation, they concurred on further enhancing bilateral policy consultations between the diplomatic authorities on regional affairs such as Africa, Asia and Middle East/West Asia and multilateral agenda including UN reform, space, maritime domains, climate change, terrorism, and the Arctic as well as policy planning.
The Ministers welcomed the growing defence and security partnership between both countries in line with the Joint Declaration on Security Cooperation, adopted at the last Annual Summit in August 2025. Minister Motegi and Minister Koizumi explained the ongoing efforts to revise Japan’s National Security Strategy, National Defence Strategy, and Defence Buildup Program, which would contribute to enhanced cooperation with India to maintain peace and security in the region and beyond.
The Ministers expressed satisfaction at the expansion and deepening of bilateral exercises, including the two air services, following the first-ever visit to India by Japan Air Self-Defence Force fighter aircraft during the India-Japan Air Force exercise “Veer Guardian 26”, as well as the visit to India by the Chief of Staff of the Air Self-Defence Force conducted in conjunction with the exercise. They concurred on further deepening cooperation in bilateral exercises through enhanced complexities, integration of unmanned systems and pursuing bilateral and multilateral exercises at short notice. They welcomed the signing of LOI (Letter of Intent) toward the utilization of firing ranges in India, whereby Japan Self-Defence Forces would, for the first time, conduct live-fire training etc., including those involving surface-to-ship missiles, at firing ranges in India. They concurred on accelerating coordination between the defence authorities of the two countries toward its early realization.
The Ministers expressed their expectation for an early formulation of the UNICORN related arrangements, and the Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) by India by February 2027 and looked forward to further strengthening of defence industrial cooperation under the framework of "Design with Japan, Make in India". They welcomed the convening of the 3rd India-Japan Defence Industries Forum in Tokyo in October 2026.
Welcoming the recently signed Memorandum of Arrangement on Maritime Security Cooperation, the Ministers concurred on moving swiftly to realize concrete outcomes between the Indian Navy and the Japan Maritime Self-Defence Force to serve their respective strategic and operational needs, including cooperation in the fields of Maritime and Air Domain Awareness (MDA), Search and Rescue (SAR), Information Sharing and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR). They affirmed that defence authorities are committed to enhancing mine countermeasures capabilities and exploring the possibility of joint development in naval ship building and design. They welcomed the expanding cooperation between the two countries’ coast guards, including the 5th Coast Guard Global Summit (CGGS) to be held in India in February 2027, a framework which was initiated by the Japan Coast Guard.
The Ministers concurred on holding a dialogue between the consular authorities of India and Japan to discuss a wide range of consular-related matters, including holding a tabletop exercise (TTX) regarding cooperation on assistance of their respective nationals abroad.
The Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening secure and resilient digital connectivity in the Indo-Pacific. They concurred on enhancing bilateral cooperation in developing trusted, redundant and high-speed undersea cable networks, including through industry partnerships, and to share best practices for ensuring the security, reliability and resilience of critical undersea communications infrastructure.
Taking note of the increasing incidence of cyber-attacks, the Ministers concurred on the need to strengthen cybersecurity cooperation, including on AI-enabled cybersecurity and the security of AI systems, with particular attention to critical infrastructure. They directed their teams to renew the existing Memorandum of Cooperation in the field of Cybersecurity and convene the next edition of the India-Japan Cyber Dialogue at an early date.
The Ministers concurred on expanding cooperation in the space field, including in Space Situational Awareness (SSA), the use of space for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA), space-related international rules and norms, and other areas of mutual interest. They concurred on the need to hold the next edition of the India-Japan Space Dialogue at an early date.
Recognising the synergies between India-Japan bilateral cooperation and the Quad's four priority areas, namely maritime and transnational security, economic prosperity and security, maritime and transnational security, critical and emerging technologies, and humanitarian assistance and emergency response, the Ministers underscored their commitment to leveraging bilateral cooperation to complement and reinforce Quad initiatives and deliver tangible benefits to partners across the Indo-Pacific. In this regard, they welcomed the holding of a series of Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meetings as well as the Quad Leaders’ Summit held in November 2026.
The Ministers also highlighted the importance of cooperation with ASEAN Member States to strengthen regional resilience and promote peace, stability and prosperity. In this context, they welcomed the first India-Japan-Philippines Trilateral 1.5 Dialogue this October as well as the first trilateral naval PASSEX exercise involving India, Japan and Indonesia in February 2026.
The Ministers reiterated their grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, and non-market policies and practices that result in overcapacity, which disrupt global supply chains in critical industries. They concurred on the importance of maintaining a fair competitive global environment and establishing and safeguarding resilient and reliable supply chains among like-minded partners to promote collective resilience.
Based on such views, the Ministers welcomed the adoption of the Joint Declaration on Economic Security Cooperation at the 16th Annual Summit and concurred on promoting concrete, project-based cooperation in strategic sectors, including semiconductors, critical minerals, information and communication technology, clean energy and pharmaceuticals. Welcoming the progress made under the second round of the Economic Security Dialogue and the inaugural Private-Sector Economic Security Dialogue, they encouraged closer engagement between relevant government agencies, industry and research institutions to identify opportunities for strengthening resilient and diversified supply chains and reducing strategic vulnerabilities. They concurred on the early convening of the inaugural meeting of the Track 1.5 Dialogue and the Follow-up Mechanism.
The Ministers affirmed that India and Japan are strategic research and development partners in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI). They welcomed the adoption of the India-Japan Joint Statement on cooperation in the Field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the Leaders’ Summit Meeting and concurred on further deepening cooperation on the AI ecosystem under the "Japan-India AI Cooperation Initiative (JAI)." They confirmed to cooperate to enhance the national capability of both countries and called for accelerating co-creation of the AI ecosystem to address their strategic, economic, and societal priorities.

hotspot mitigation

content:
The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed the incorporation of Good Storage and Distribution Practices (GSDP) guidelines for pharmaceutical products into the Drugs Rules, 1945. The proposal aims to ensure that the quality, safety, efficacy and integrity of pharmaceutical products are maintained throughout the distribution chain, from the manufacturer or importer to the point of supply to the patient.
The proposed framework builds upon the GSDP guidance developed by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO). The guidelines seek to ensure the quality and identity of pharmaceutical products at every stage of the distribution process, including procurement, purchasing, storage, distribution, transportation, documentation and record-keeping.
Maintaining appropriate storage and distribution conditions is essential to preserving the quality and integrity of pharmaceutical products beyond the manufacturing stage. The proposed GSDP framework seeks to address potential risks associated with their handling and movement across the supply chain, including deterioration, contamination, mix-ups, falsification, diversion and unauthorised distribution.
The incorporation of GSDP requirements into the Drugs Rules, 1945, is expected to strengthen the regulatory framework governing pharmaceutical distribution and support effective regulatory oversight, inspection and enforcement by the Central and State drug-control authorities. It will also promote robust documentation, record-keeping and traceability, while enhancing accountability among manufacturers, importers, wholesalers, distributors, stockists and other entities involved in the distribution process.
The proposed guidelines will further strengthen assurance that pharmaceutical products remain within specified quality and environmental conditions during storage and transportation, thereby reducing the risk of deterioration, contamination, mix-ups, falsification, diversion and unauthorised distribution. This will support the availability of pharmaceutical products of assured quality to patients and healthcare providers.
The proposed amendment represents an important step towards strengthening India's pharmaceutical quality-management system and ensuring that the quality established at the manufacturing stage is maintained throughout the supply chain until the product reaches the patient.

content:
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed an amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945, through a draft Gazette Notification G.S.R. 985 (E) dated 6th November, published in the Gazette of India to provide regulatory flexibility under the revised Schedule M for certain categories of drugs, namely medicinal gases, empty gelatin capsules and disinfectant fluids.
The proposed amendment follows representations received from stakeholders regarding the applicability of certain provisions of the revised Schedule M, notified vide G.S.R. 922(E) dated 28 December 2023, to these categories of products.
The matter was deliberated in detail by the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) during its 93rd meeting held on 16 February 2026. The Board observed that certain requirements under the revised Schedule M may not be relevant to the manufacturing processes of medicinal gases, empty gelatin capsules and disinfectant fluids. Accordingly, it recommended the continuation of exemptions that were available to these categories under Schedule M prior to its revision.
The proposed amendment seeks to ensure that regulatory requirements are appropriately aligned with the nature and manufacturing processes of specific categories of drugs, while maintaining effective regulatory oversight. It also provides for Licensing Authorities to take product-specific decisions based on relevant scientific and practical considerations.

content:
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed an amendment to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, through a draft Gazette Notification G.S.R. 983 (E) dated 6th November, to include ‘antimicrobials’ in the definition of ‘New Drug’ under Rule 2(1)(w)(v).
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global public health concern and a priority requiring coordinated action. The G20 New Delhi Leaders’ Declaration also underscored the need to address antimicrobial resistance through a One Health approach.
The proposed amendment has been initiated in view of concerns regarding the grant of manufacturing licences for antimicrobial products without adequate regulatory scrutiny, including the requirement for studies such as bioavailability/bioequivalence and stability studies. The absence of such assessments may affect the quality, safety and efficacy of antimicrobial products. Substandard or ineffective antimicrobials can contribute to the development and spread of antimicrobial resistance, posing risks to patient safety.
The proposed amendment seeks to bring antimicrobials within the regulatory framework applicable to new drugs under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019. Accordingly, manufacturers would be required to obtain permission from the Central Licensing Authority (CLA) before applying for a manufacturing licence from the concerned State Licensing Authority (SLA). This is expected to strengthen central regulatory oversight and help ensure the quality, safety and efficacy of antimicrobial products.
The draft notification has been issued to invite objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public before the proposed amendment is considered for finalisation by the Central Government.

title: Union Ministry of Health Proposes Separate Licensing Framework for Wholesale of Bulk Drugs
subtitle: Proposed Amendments to Drugs Rules, 1945, to Enhance Accountability and Control in Bulk Drug Distribution; strengthen Supply Chain Oversight
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

content:
The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, vide Draft Gazette Notification G.S.R. No. 987 (E) dated 2nd November, 2026, to introduce a separate application form (Form 19-BC) and licence form (Form 20-BC) for the sale of bulk drugs (active or inactive bulk substances), distinct from the existing licensing provisions for formulations.
At present, a common licence covers the wholesale sale of both formulations and bulk drugs. The proposed amendment seeks to establish a dedicated licensing framework for bulk drugs, enabling more focused regulatory oversight of their wholesale sale and greater accountability in the pharmaceutical supply chain. The proposal was agreed upon by the Drugs Consultative Committee (DCC) in its 67th meeting held on 17 November 2025, and by the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) in its 93rd meeting held on 16 February 2026.
Under the proposed framework, the licence will capture the categories of bulk drugs handled by wholesalers, including drugs covered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. The sale of bulk drugs will be carried out under the personal supervision of a competent person, thereby strengthening accountability in their distribution and handling.
Upon implementation, the proposed amendment will:
Give better control over the sale of bulk drugs by way of wholesale.
Strengthen enforcement control in relation to antimicrobial resistance and the movement of NDPS drugs.
Require wholesalers of bulk drugs to obtain a separate licence for sale.
To facilitate the transition to the revised licensing requirements, existing licensees will be provided adequate time to comply with the new provisions. The requirements will become applicable to them upon expiry of their current retention period or 12 months after the final publication of the amendment, whichever is later.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the inaugural session of two-day counter-terrorism conference organised in New Delhi. On the occasion, Union Home Minister released the publication ‘Fail-Safe Investigation’ brought out by National Investigation Agency (NIA). He also laid the foundation stone of NIA office complex in Chandigarh and inaugurated NIA residential complex built at Maidangarhi in Delhi. In addition, Union Home Minister e-launched the NIA’s ‘Pushti’ portal and conferred decorations on s
even
officers and personnel of the National Investigation Agency.
On this occasion, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Union Home Secretary Shri Govind Mohan, Director Intelligence Bureau (IB) Dr. Mahesh Dikshit, Special Secretary (Internal Security) in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Anand Swarup, and Director General National Investigation Agency (NIA) Shri Rakesh Aggarwal, along with several other senior officers, were present. Senior police officers from the states and Union Territories, officers from counter-terrorism agencies, and experts from related fields including law, forensics and technology are participating in this conference.
Addressing the conference, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that India has been a victim of terrorism and we have been confronting terrorism for a long time. He noted that police forces of different states had made various kinds of efforts, but a lack of coordinated action was clearly visible. Over time, during the tenures of successive governments, gradual efforts were made to overcome these shortcomings. Today, we can say with satisfaction that in this vast country — from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Dwarka to Kamakhya — we are putting in place a system under which a uniform strategy to combat terrorism will operate right down to the level of every police station.
Shri Amit Shah said that some successful operations have recently been carried out against terrorism, which has strengthened the confidence of our country. He stated that just yesterday we achieved a significant milestone in the fight against terrorism. With the elimination of Lashkar terrorist Latif Bhat, the entire Kashmir has become free from the presence of India-born terrorists. Shri Shah noted that this situation has come about after 35 years.
Shri Amit Shah said that the Shahzad Bhatti network has been declared a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). More than 40 of its modules have been neutralised across the country. In the action taken against this network, over 100 cases have been registered and more than 271 arrests have been made. Shri Shah stated that the hallmark of a successful agency is to apprehend terrorists and put them behind bars even before they can execute a terrorist incident. He said that the police of every state should analyse this model, accept it, and implement it in their respective areas.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that since 2019 we have launched a special drive to bring fugitives back to India, and so far 303 fugitives have been brought back from 36 countries, thereby strengthening the security of our nation. He noted that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Ministry of Home Affairs have made special efforts in this regard. Our intelligence agencies have made outstanding efforts in bringing back fugitives living abroad through scientific methods. Shri Shah stated that if we are to completely eliminate the three menaces— terrorism, organised crime and drugs, it is essential to bring the culprits and masterminds who have taken shelter abroad before Indian courts.
Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we have adopted ‘Zero Tolerance’ policy against terrorism, and positive results of this are being achieved. He stated that, as part of continuous efforts in this direction, NIA Act was first amended on 2nd August 2019. New offences were brought under the jurisdiction of NIA and additional jurisdictions were granted to it. Shri Shah added  that UAPA was amended on 14th August 2019, under which NIA was empowered to seize the properties of terrorists and a process was initiated to declare individuals as terrorists. Union Home Minister noted that in September 2019 a unified action plan was prepared to counter radicalisation, which was finalised in December 2019 after discussions with various ministries. In September 2022, PFI network was dismantled. He said that the destruction of PFI network is a striking example of how effective a joint operation by the Indian police can be. In a single night, coordinated action was carried out simultaneously in 11 states, completely dismantling the entire PFI network and breaking its backbone. By destroying the PFI network, we have preemptively eliminated several serious problems that the country could have faced in the future. He added that the dismantling of PFI network is the key to preventing many potential incidents that could have occurred in the times to come.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the functioning of the Multi-Agency Centre (MAC) has been reorganised. Cyber security, narcotics, organised crime networks and emerging radicalisation hotspots have been brought under the purview of the MAC. In 2023, the methodology of the MAC was restructured using state-of-the-art technology. A National Memory Bank was established and efforts were made to create a centralised database. He further stated that during this period, not only were the legal powers of NIA enhanced, but its national character was also expanded. Almost simultaneously, 16 new branch offices and two zonal offices were approved. NIA was empowered to conduct investigations for the protection of the interests of Indians residing abroad. A ban was imposed on the glorification of terrorism. A 25-point integrated action plan was formulated to control the funding of terrorists, and this is being effectively monitored.
Shri Amit Shah said, NIA officers have been trained to gain international exposure, and 70 new NIA Special Courts have been established across the country. He stated that peace had been established in three major hotspots, networks such as PFI and Shahzad Bhatti had been dismantled, and a scientific mechanism had been developed to bring back fugitives from abroad. He also highlighted the implementation of a new comprehensive approach to border security, the complete removal of illegal religious structures along the borders, and improved coordination among various agencies to strengthen economic security. Shri Shah stated that the government had worked simultaneously and effectively on all these fronts.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated that we are moving forward with an ecosystem-based approach to combating terrorism through cooperation between the Centre and the States, and that this cooperation needs to be further strengthened. He said that we have strengthened the provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) on the legal front, and that the flow of information needs to be made smoother and more robust at the institutional level. He emphasised that we must also change our work culture to achieve victory in this fight. On the operational front, agencies must enhance their capabilities while also undertaking modernisation. We must target the entire chain of terror financing, which requires better coordination with financial investigation agencies. Shri Shah stated that we will not achieve success unless we strike at the entire terrorist network in a coordinated and comprehensive manner.
Shri Amit Shah stated that in the fight against terrorism, our approach must be based on shared and collective goals, along with clearly defined accountability. He emphasised that unless our goals are shared and accountability for achieving them is clearly established, success cannot be achieved. He further said that this conference must be made outcome-oriented, which will be possible only when all participants make concerted efforts in this direction.
Union Home Minister said that India needs to strengthen the concept of proactive action in its counter-terrorism policy, with greater emphasis on structural and operational capabilities. Shri Amit Shah stated that the entire terrorist network must be investigated and its capabilities dismantled. He said that by investigating the entire network, many incidents could be prevented before they occur. Shri Shah emphasised the need to develop a mechanism through which police station-level intelligence is transmitted through multiple levels to the Director General of Police (DGP), enabling the extraction of actionable intelligence. He also said that the Anti-Terrorism Squads (ATS) of every state need to strengthen their cyber expert units, as technology is increasingly being used in such crimes. Union Home Minister further stated that establishing a Quadrangular Regional Security Grid in Border States should be a key priority. He also stressed the need to enhance the capabilities of the ATS units across all states.

title: WAVES Film Bazaar Marks 20 Years of Fostering Global Film Collaborations
subtitle: 20th edition to connect Indian filmmakers with global markets; inaugural ceremony to be held in Goa tomorrow
content:
Goa, 19 November 2026
From a modest gathering of 204 delegates from 18 countries in 2007 to a major international marketplace welcoming over 2,500 delegates from more than 40 countries in 2025, Film Bazaar has evolved into an important platform connecting Indian cinema with the global film industry. Marking its 20th year, WAVES Film Bazaar 2026 celebrates two decades of fostering creative collaborations, discovering new stories and opening global opportunities for Indian cinema.
Organised by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, as part of International Film Festival of India (IFFI), WAVES Film Bazaar is part of the broader World Audio Visual and Entertainment Summit (WAVES) initiative. Guided by the vision of ‘Create in India, Create for the World’, the platform seeks to translate India's creative potential into global opportunities through co-production, financing, distribution and international partnerships.
The 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar will be inaugurated on 20 November 2026 at The Ballroom, Taj Cidade de Goa Horizon. Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, will deliver the welcome address, followed by the Guest of Honour address by Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director. Shri G. Krishnakumar, Chairman, NFDC, will deliver the inaugural address, while Shri Prabhat Kumar, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, will propose the vote of thanks. Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director, NFDC, will also be present. The formal proceedings will be followed by a presentation on ‘Navigating WAVES Film Bazaar’ by the Film Bazaar team.
A marketplace for stories and opportunities
Over two decades, Film Bazaar has evolved from a networking event into a structured marketplace connecting filmmakers, producers, investors, distributors, sales agents and festival programmers. Its programmes support films at various stages of development through initiatives such as the NFDC Screenwriters’ Lab, Co-Production Market and Work-in-Progress Lab. The Viewing Room, Market Screenings, curated B2B meetings and Knowledge Series further facilitate project discovery, industry engagement and potential collaborations.
The 2025 edition, held in Goa from 20 to 24 November alongside the 56th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), brought together over 2,500 delegates from more than 40 countries. It showcased 320 projects and facilitated over 1,200 one-to-one business meetings involving more than 220 buyers. Business discussions and negotiations were valued at approximately ₹1,050 crore, including MoUs worth around ₹100 crore reported on the sidelines of the event.
WAVES Bazaar: Extending India's creative reach beyond the annual marketplace
The WAVES initiative extends beyond the annual Film Bazaar through WAVES Bazaar, a year-round international B2B platform launched in January 2025. Covering film, television, OTT, animation, VFX, gaming, music and other creative sectors, it connects creators and businesses with potential buyers and collaborators.
According to the October 2026 progress note, WAVES Bazaar had over 12,500 active users, including more than 5,000 buyers and approximately 6,500 sellers, with over 2,800 active projects. AI-enabled semantic search, matchmaking, virtual pitching and online B2B meeting facilities help creators and businesses identify potential partners and sustain industry engagement beyond physical events.
Its international outreach across countries such as Australia, Japan, South Korea, Italy, Germany, Canada, France and Spain has further expanded avenues for Indian creative enterprises. Participation in global industry platforms, including Gamescom, the Toronto International Film Festival, Venice and MIPCOM, has strengthened engagement with international stakeholders.
These initiatives reflect a broader effort to take Indian creativity from ‘Craft to Commerce’, strengthening India's position as a global hub for content creation, intellectual property and creative industries.
As WAVES Film Bazaar marks two decades of its journey, it continues to serve as an important platform for independent filmmakers, regional-language cinema and emerging creative talent to access international markets, forge partnerships and take Indian stories to audiences across the world.

The Press Information Bureau (PIB), in collaboration with the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), organised a Film Appreciation Course for accredited media delegates and students of mass communication ahead of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026. content:
Goa 19 November 2026
The grand Opening ceremony to bring together filmmakers, artists and delegates from India and abroad for an evening of music, cultural performances and cinematic celebration under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’
Goa is all set to welcome filmmakers, artists, delegates and cinema enthusiasts from India and across the world as the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) commences tomorrow, November 20, bringing together the world of cinema for nine days of films, cultural exchange and creative engagement.
Organized under the theme
‘Stories Without Borders’
, this year’s festival will bring together films and creative voices from different countries, cultures and cinematic traditions, celebrating the universal language of cinema.
The opening ceremony at Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Stadium, Goa, will feature musical presentations, cultural performances and ceremonial proceedings, marking the commencement of the nine-day festival.
The ceremony will begin with a sound and light presentation, followed by the National Song and National Anthem. The ceremonial opening will include the lighting of the lamp and watering of the Tulsi plant, symbolising light, life and new beginnings.
Prominent personalities at the opening ceremony
The ceremony will feature addresses by the Chief Minister of Goa, Dr. Pramod Sawant, and senior dignitaries from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
The opening ceremony will also bring together prominent personalities from Indian cinema, including Member of Parliament Ravi Kishan, filmmaker and Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker, filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar and filmmaker Aanand L. Rai, among other distinguished members of the Indian and international film fraternity.
Ricky Kej's symphonic orchestra
A major highlight of the evening will be a symphonic orchestra presentation by three-time Grammy Award-winning composer and environmentalist Ricky Kej, titled
‘A World of Cinema Through Music’
. The performance will bring alive the universal language of cinema through a musical journey across cultures and storytelling traditions.
The musical presentation will be followed by
‘Music Without Borders’
, bringing together musicians from different countries in a celebration of musical traditions, harmony and cultural exchange, reflecting the festival's theme.
The peacock motif associated with IFFI will come alive through
‘Beyond the Frame’
, a special dance presentation, bringing the festival's iconic emblem to life through movement and artistic expression.
The ceremony will also feature the felicitation of the Indian Panorama and International Competition juries, recognising the filmmakers and cinema professionals entrusted with selecting films for the festival's competitive sections.
International Competition Jury
The International Competition Jury will be chaired by filmmaker Aanand L. Rai and will comprise distinguished cinema professionals from across the world, including Sol Berruezo Pichon-Rivière (Argentina), Bogdan Muresanu (Romania), María Alejandra Rojas (Colombia) and Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke (Thailand). The jury will be felicitated during the opening ceremony.
Indian Panorama Jury
The Feature Film Jury is chaired by National Award-winning filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar, while the Non-Feature Film Jury is chaired by filmmaker and former Director of the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, Himansu Sekhar Khatua.
A special presentation marking two decades of WAVES Film Bazaar will showcase its evolution as a platform connecting Indian filmmakers with the international film industry and facilitating creative and business collaborations.
Nine days of cinema from across the world
From acclaimed international films to emerging voices and diverse Indian stories, IFFI 2026 will offer audiences a wide-ranging cinematic experience. The festival will screen over 150 international films from 86 countries, bringing diverse storytelling traditions and perspectives to Goa.
The festival will open with
Fatherland
, directed by acclaimed Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski, whose work received the Best Director Award at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. The Mid-Fest Film will be
I Matter
, directed by Alina Șerban, a Romania-Germany-Belgium co-production featuring dialogues in Romanian and Romani. The festival will conclude with
We Are All Strangers
, directed by Singaporean filmmaker Anthony Chen, bringing the nine-day celebration of world cinema to a close on 28th November. The festival will also spotlight international cinema through competitions, curated showcases and country presentations, with Spain as the Country of Honour and Russia as the Partner Country.
Indian cinema will find a prominent place through Indian Panorama, featuring 76 films in 18 languages. A special focus on BRICS cinema will further bring films from member and partner countries into the spotlight.
The festival will celebrate emerging filmmakers through the Best Debut Feature Films Competition, alongside other competitive sections, including the International Competition and ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal, recognising cinematic excellence across diverse categories.
New Segments in IFFI 2026
This year’s festival introduces two new segments to broaden its cinematic offerings and celebrate diverse forms of storytelling. The first segment,
Animation
, will feature five outstanding films, showcasing creativity and innovation in animated cinema. The second segment,
Films About Films
, presents five films with the objective of bringing the art and craft of filmmaking to the forefront.
Golden Peacock and Silver Peacock Awards
The festival's competitive sections will recognise cinematic excellence through the prestigious Golden Peacock and Silver Peacock Awards, comprising six awards. The festival will also present the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal for a film promoting tolerance, intercultural dialogue and a culture of peace.

content:

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) will draw its curtains with ‘
We Are All Strangers’
, a compelling feature film by acclaimed Singaporean filmmaker Anthony Chen. A 2026 Singaporean production, the film will be screened as the festival’s Closing Film, offering audiences an evocative cinematic exploration of human relationships, familial ties and the complexities of contemporary life.
Set against the textured backdrop of contemporary Singapore,
We Are All Strangers

Simultaneously, the arrival of a spirited woman in the life of Junyang’s hardworking father subtly alters the unspoken equilibrium between father and son. title: Nurturing tomorrow’s filmmakers: CMOT brings 100 young creative talents to 57th IFFI
subtitle: Sixth edition of the initiative to spotlight 13 filmmaking crafts, 48-hour challenge and Talent Camp to offer hands-on industry exposure
content:
Goa, 19 November 2026
Behind every film that reaches the screen is a team of creative minds whose contributions shape its story, sound and visual identity. Recognising the importance of this collective talent, Creative Minds of Tomorrow (CMOT), an initiative of the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting implemented by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), returns for its sixth edition at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), Goa, with 100 young talents from across India.
The 2026 cohort brings together aspiring professionals from 13 filmmaking crafts, spanning direction, acting, cinematography, editing and subtitling, scriptwriting, playback singing, music composition, sound recording, costume design, hair and makeup, art direction, animation, visual effects (VFX), augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and voice-over and dubbing. By bringing together participants from different creative disciplines, the initiative places collaboration at the centre of the filmmaking experience.
The selection process combines perspectives from film education and industry practice. A 13-member Selection Jury comprising faculty members from the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) evaluates applications across the respective crafts. The next stage is undertaken by a 12-member Grand Jury of established industry practitioners, which identifies the selected participants. The filmmaking challenge and its final awards are subsequently evaluated by a five-member Great Grand Jury comprising distinguished film professionals.
A key component of the programme is the 48-Hour Filmmaking Challenge, conducted by FTII, Pune, in collaboration with NFDC. Participants from different crafts will work together to conceptualise and produce short films within a 48-hour production window. Supported by expert mentorship and institutional guidance, the challenge offers an intensive practical experience of working as a filmmaking team under professional production constraints. The completed films will be screened specially at IFFI and evaluated by an eminent jury of film industry professionals, with awards recognising excellence across categories.
The CMOT Talent Camp will further connect participants with the wider media and entertainment industry, bringing them in contact with production houses, studios, music labels, OTT platforms, broadcasters and other industry stakeholders. It will enable young creators to present their original work, interact with industry representatives and explore professional opportunities.
Since its inception in 2021, CMOT has developed into a platform connecting emerging creative professionals with the media and entertainment industry. Its alumni have gone on to work on international productions and receive recognition at platforms and festivals including Cannes, the Berlinale, the Toronto International Film Festival and the International Emmy Awards.
As India’s creative economy continues to grow, nurturing skilled and innovative professionals across filmmaking disciplines becomes increasingly important. By combining learning, practical collaboration and industry engagement, CMOT seeks to create pathways for emerging talent to translate creative ability into professional opportunities.
For the 100 participants arriving in Goa, IFFI will be more than a showcase of world cinema. It will be an opportunity to collaborate, learn and take their first steps towards shaping the future of Indian filmmaking.

title: Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation Organises 14th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad
subtitle: Four Districts from Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Assam and Tripura Showcase Innovative Practices on Community Ownership, Skilling, O&M, Source Sustainability and 24x7 Rural Water Supply under JJM 2.0
date:

content:
The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised the
14th edition
of the
District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad
today through video conferencing, bringing together senior officials, District Collectors/ District Magistrates, and Mission Directors of State/UTs to deliberate on accelerating the implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and sharing of best practices.
The Samvad was chaired Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM).  Senior Officers from DDWS and National Project Monitoring Units were also present.
In his opening remarks,
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM
, highlighted that the District Collectors' Peyjal Samvad has evolved into an important platform for sharing grassroots innovations and district-level experiences from across the country. He emphasised that the good practices presented during the Samvad are compiled and shared with key institutions, including the Prime Minister's Office, Cabinet Secretariat, NITI Aayog and other stakeholder ministries to facilitate wider replication and policy learning.
He urged District Collectors to ensure regular monthly meetings of District Water and Sanitation Committees (DWSCs), active use of the Decision Support System (DSS) for evidence-based planning, and review of gaps identified during the Jal Seva Aankalan through district-level improvement plans (DIP). He also called upon States and districts to leverage opportunities under the 16th Finance Commission, strengthen community participation and promote skill development through government institutions and setups like ITIs, RSETIs, SRLMs for sustaining rural water supply infrastructure created under Jal Jeevan Mission.
Ms. Pooja Bhatt, Director, NJJM,
made a presentation on
Skilling under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
. Highlighting the employment potential emerging from the rural drinking water sector, she shared that studies have indicated significant opportunities for creation of skilled local workforces for operation and maintenance of water supply systems. She elaborated on the proposed framework involving Jal Jeevan Mitras, multi-skill technicians, diploma operators and supervisory personnel, supported by district-level technical units. She also highlighted the Sujalam Shakti initiative, which seeks to empower women to play a greater role in water quality surveillance, community mobilisation and protection of water assets.
The presentation also stressed the importance of strengthening local capacities through structured training programmes, convergence with government training institutions and refresher training for field-level personnel to ensure long-term sustainability of drinking water infrastructure.
Innovative Best Practices Shared by Districts Through Presentations
During the Peyjal Samvad, a total of four districts presented their progress and best field practices which will further help other State’s districts to develop better under JJM 2.0. Each presentation was delivered by the respective District Collector/ District Magistrate.
Kangra Nagar, Himachal Pradesh – Sh. Hemraj Bairwa, Deputy Commissioner
presented the district's efforts towards ensuring sustainable drinking water services in a geographically challenging Himalayan region. He informed that the district has achieved 100% coverage and also has made considerable progress in Har Ghar Jal certification, with certification processes continuing for the remaining villages. The presentation highlighted challenges arising from difficult terrain, scattered habitations, power constraints, ageing distribution systems, monsoon-related disruptions and operation and maintenance requirements. To address these challenges, Kangra has prioritised revival and augmentation of older schemes, strengthening of pumping systems, creation of additional storage infrastructure and implementation of source sustainability measures. The district also showcased its extensive water quality surveillance network and community engagement through VWSCs, training of women members, awareness campaigns. Preventive maintenance practices, grievance redressal systems and continuous capacity building of field-level stakeholders were highlighted as key pillars of the district's strategy.
AS&MD, NJJM
emphasised the need for strengthening user charge collection mechanisms and ensuring long-term source sustainability. He suggested that Himachal Pradesh may study successful inter-departmental convergence models adopted in Uttarakhand for addressing source sustainability challenges in hilly regions. He also encouraged greater use of the Decision Support System for planning and monitoring interventions.
Valsad, Gujarat - Sh. Nitin V. Sangwan, District Collector’s
presentation focused on innovative approaches for strengthening operation and maintenance, tariff collection and skilling. He mentioned that the district has completed 100% Sujalam Bharat Ids and Sujal Gaon ID creation. The district highlighted its performance-based incentive mechanisms for Gram Panchayats, Self-Help Groups and operators, which have significantly improved user charge collection and strengthened financial sustainability of rural water supply systems. Valsad also shared experiences in promoting surface water-based drinking water systems, thereby reducing dependence on groundwater sources. The district demonstrated how targeted training programmes delivered through ITIs and vocational institutions have strengthened the technical capacities of water supply operators, Panchayats and community institutions. Community awareness programmes, regular water quality monitoring and innovative infrastructure mapping initiatives were also highlighted.
AS&MD, NJJM
appreciated Gujarat's innovative approach towards tariff collection, skilling and operation and maintenance. He emphasised the importance of continuous training and refresher programmes for village-level workers and encouraged the State to facilitate exposure visits for other States interested in learning from Gujarat's approaches to skilling and community-based management.
Jorhat, Assam – Sh. Jay Shivani, Deputy Commissioner
highlighted the district's efforts to achieve full functionality of water supply schemes, strengthen community ownership and pioneer 24x7 rural water supply systems in Assam. The district described its robust monitoring framework, decentralised O&M mechanisms and innovative practices for improving tariff collection. Jorhat reported significant progress in ensuring regular monitoring of schemes, timely repairs and strengthening the capacity of Panchayats and local institutions and also showcased innovative tariff collection models and strong community participation through Water User Committees, Jal Mitras and Jal Doots. These efforts have contributed to improving both functionality and financial sustainability of rural water supply systems.  The district shared its experience of preparing communities, strengthening local institutions and adopting a phased approach before transitioning to continuous water supply. The district’s initiative has generated valuable learnings for scaling up 24x7 rural water supply across Assam.
AS&MD, NJJM
congratulated Jorhat for pioneering 24x7 rural water supply in Assam and called upon other districts to learn from and replicate the district's best practices relating to functionality, operation and maintenance, tariff collection and community ownership. He also encouraged the district to progressively move towards saturation, beginning from villages and Gram Panchayats.
Unakoti, Tripura – Ms. Megha Jain, District Magistrate and Commissioner
presented the district's initiatives focused on Jan Bhagidari, source sustainability and strengthening drinking water service delivery in tribal and difficult terrain areas and highlighted the active involvement of Gram Panchayats, Self-Help Groups, School Water Clubs and local communities in promoting water conservation, water quality monitoring and community ownership of assets. The district also showcased convergence-based approaches for groundwater recharge, pond rejuvenation, greywater management and rainwater harvesting. Through close coordination among line departments, source sustainability measures are being integrated with drinking water service delivery interventions to ensure long-term water security.  A notable example presented during the Samvad was the development of an innovative surface water-based drinking water scheme for habitations inhabited by the Reang community, a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG). Through scientific source identification, community participation and local planning processes, the district has successfully addressed drinking water challenges in an area where groundwater-based solutions were technically unviable.
​​​​​​​
​​​​​​​
AS&MD, NJJM
appreciated the district's emphasis on source sustainability, community ownership and convergence. He stressed the importance of post-monsoon water quality testing and directed all States and districts to ensure regular water quality surveillance to safeguard public health.
The deliberations during the 14th District Collectors' Peyjal Samvad demonstrated how districts across the country are adopting innovative and locally suited approaches to strengthen drinking water service delivery. The sharing of these experiences is expected to support wider replication of successful practices and further accelerate progress towards the vision of Har Ghar Jal and sustainable rural water supply across India.

title: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya chairs 240th meeting of Central Board of Trustees (CBT), EPF
subtitle:
CBT approves Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF members, enabling periodic payouts of retirement savings

The Board approves major relaxation in EPF withdrawal: Minimum PF balance requirement reduced from 25% to 10% and waiting period for final withdrawal from 12 months to 2 months

EDLI exemption reforms: Relief and transitional support for establishments under the Scheme
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 NOV 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, chaired the 240th meeting of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT), Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) in New Delhi today. Co-Vice-Chairperson Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar (Secretary, Labour & Employment), and Member Secretary Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi (CPFC), alongside representatives of Central/State Governments, employers and employees, also attended the meeting.
The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), in recent years, has introduced several key reforms and innovations to
strengthen social security delivery through wider coverage, simplified claim settlement and digitalisation. These include enhancement in wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage from
₹15,000 to ₹25,000,
introduction of simplified partial withdrawal rules
and
liberalised withdrawal limits,
and rolling out of CITES 2.01, among others. With a view to taking this spirit of reform further, several key proposals were put forth by EPFO in today’s meeting, chaired by Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya.
The following agenda items were placed before the Board, relating to pension reforms, provident fund flexibility, investment management, governance, exemption policy and digital transformation of EPFO:-
Introduction of Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF Members:
The Board approved a proposal to introduce Systematic Withdrawal Plan, which will enable retiring EPF members to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic instalments instead of withdrawing the entire amount in one go.
This reform will enable retiring members to withdraw their accumulated provident fund savings at regular intervals, such as monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, based on their preference. This facility would provide members with a structured source of periodic income while allowing the remaining corpus to continue generating returns, thereby helping augment their retirement income and supplement their pension benefits. The facility would be entirely voluntary, with no compulsion on members to opt for withdrawals. The option may also be extended to eligible family members/beneficiaries, ensuring greater flexibility and financial security for the family. This aims to ensure stable post-retirement income, reduce reinvestment risks, strengthen fund sustainability and facilitate the extension of social security coverage to gig and platform workers.
SWP will enable members to convert their retirement savings into a stable and predictable stream of systematic withdrawals post-retirement, while preserving ownership of the underlying corpus. Approximately 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years possess provident fund accumulations exceeding ₹5 lakh are expected to be the primary beneficiaries of the proposed SWP framework during the initial phase. In case of the member's death during the payout period, the nominee or dependent will be able to withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments. The initiative will enhance retirement financial security by providing members with a flexible, regular and reliable income stream, while safeguarding their families' interests. Apart from the immediate potential beneficiaries indicated above, the SWP scheme is likely to attract many other PF members retiring in the future who seek an additional post-retirement stream of withdrawals from their accumulated PF corpus.
Additionally, to further boost flexibility and
move towards the goal of universal social security
, the proposal also introduces UAN-linked mechanisms for direct voluntary contributions and third-party micro-contributions (such as customer tips), completely independent of traditional employer payroll systems. The necessary amendments
to the EPF
scheme will be notified accordingly after approval
from the Ministry
. The proposal
for a corresponding
amendment
in the Income
Tax Act is being taken up with the Ministry of Finance.
Review of minimum balance and waiting period for final PF withdrawal:
Board approved the provisions relating to the minimum balance requirement and waiting period for withdrawal, with a view to safeguarding the long-term social security interests of EPF members. A provision had earlier been made for earmarking 25% of the contributions in the Members’ account as Minimum Balance to be maintained by the member at all times. Now, the minimum balance requirement  for EPF  has been reduced from existing 25% to 10% and waiting period has been reduced from 12 months to 2 months. The changes aim to provide greater financial flexibility to EPF members while safeguarding their long-term social security interests.
Relief in EDLI exemption cases:
The Board approved amendments to EDLI Scheme, 2026, to facilitate resolution of pending legacy exemption cases and provide a six-month window to eligible establishments for renewal of expired exemptions, along with relief from contributions, interest and penal damages for the verified transitional period. This will provide relief to eligible establishments by facilitating the settlement of pending and expired exemption cases, with a six-month window for renewal and relaxation from contributions, interest and penal damages for the verified transitional period.
The proposed amendments aim to resolve long-pending exemption cases under the earlier EDLI Scheme, 1976, and address difficulties faced by establishments during the transition to the new Scheme. This will help establishments that had been maintaining group insurance policies for their employees but could not complete formal exemption or renewal procedures due to administrative and procedural difficulties.
Establishments that maintained continuous group insurance coverage with benefits equal to or better than the statutory EDLI Scheme and duly settled eligible insurance claims may receive relief from contribution liability for the intervening period, along with protection from penal damages and interest, subject to verification. This initiative reflects the Government's commitment to reducing compliance difficulties, ensuring a fair transition to the new legal framework and providing relief to establishments while safeguarding employees' insurance benefits.
Investment in Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs):
The Board in-principle approved to permit investment of up to 3% of fresh accretion in eligible Alternative Investment Funds, within the existing overall investment ceiling, initially through government-backed entities. The decision aims to diversify EPFO's investment portfolio while ensuring prescribed safeguards and investment oversight.
Surrender/cancellation of EPF exemptions
: Proposals concerning surrender of exemption by 27 establishments and cancellation of exemption in four establishments were reviewed. These cases involve transfer of accumulated provident fund savings amounting to approximately ₹5,996 crore to EPFO, covering 1,44,437 members, bringing their accounts under EPFO's direct administration.
Implementation of CITES 2.0:
The Board was apprised of the progress of Centralised IT Enabled System (CITES) 2.0, a centralised, UAN-based digital platform developed by C-DAC to modernise EPFO services. Post implementation of CITIES 2.0 auto-processing of claims increased from 39% to 71% of the total claim processed. The introduction of pre-validation greater automation and simplified withdrawal limits reduced overall rejection ratio from 23% to 7.82%. The overall processing and the average claims settlement time has declined from 11.15 days to 2.57 days.
Budget Estimates 2026-27 and 2027-28 of EPFO:
The Board approved Revised Estimates for 2026-27 and Budget Estimates for 2027-28 of EPFO under EPF, EPS and EDLI Schemes, covering projected receipts, income and expenditure, to ensure effective financial planning and management of EPFO funds.
The proposals placed before the CBT meeting, underline EPFO's commitment to strengthening the country's social security framework, providing greater flexibility in accessing retirement savings, ensuring sustainable pension administration, safeguarding members' investments and delivering technology-driven, transparent and efficient services to EPF members and pensioners.

Co-Vice-Chairperson Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar (Secretary, Labour & Employment), and Member Secretary Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi (CPFC), alongside representatives of Central/State Governments, employers and employees, also attended the meeting.
The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), in recent years, has introduced several key reforms and innovations to
strengthen social security delivery through wider coverage, simplified claim settlement and digitalisation. These include enhancement in wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage from
₹15,000 to ₹25,000,
introduction of simplified partial withdrawal rules
and
liberalised withdrawal limits,
and rolling out of CITES 2.01, among others. With a view to taking this spirit of reform further, several key proposals were put forth by EPFO in today’s meeting, chaired by Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya.
The following agenda items were placed before the Board, relating to pension reforms, provident fund flexibility, investment management, governance, exemption policy and digital transformation of EPFO:-
Introduction of Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF Members:
The Board approved a proposal to introduce Systematic Withdrawal Plan, which will enable retiring EPF members to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic instalments instead of withdrawing the entire amount in one go.
This reform will enable retiring members to withdraw their accumulated provident fund savings at regular intervals, such as monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, based on their preference. This facility would provide members with a structured source of periodic income while allowing the remaining corpus to continue generating returns, thereby helping augment their retirement income and supplement their pension benefits. The facility would be entirely voluntary, with no compulsion on members to opt for withdrawals. The option may also be extended to eligible family members/beneficiaries, ensuring greater flexibility and financial security for the family. This aims to ensure stable post-retirement income, reduce reinvestment risks, strengthen fund sustainability and facilitate the extension of social security coverage to gig and platform workers.
SWP will enable members to convert their retirement savings into a stable and predictable stream of systematic withdrawals post-retirement, while preserving ownership of the underlying corpus. Approximately 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years possess provident fund accumulations exceeding ₹5 lakh are expected to be the primary beneficiaries of the proposed SWP framework during the initial phase. In case of the member's death during the payout period, the nominee or dependent will be able to withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments. The initiative will enhance retirement financial security by providing members with a flexible, regular and reliable income stream, while safeguarding their families' interests. Apart from the immediate potential beneficiaries indicated above, the SWP scheme is likely to attract many other PF members retiring in the future who seek an additional post-retirement stream of withdrawals from their accumulated PF corpus.
Additionally, to further boost flexibility and
move towards the goal of universal social security
, the proposal also introduces UAN-linked mechanisms for direct voluntary contributions and third-party micro-contributions (such as customer tips), completely independent of traditional employer payroll systems. The necessary amendments
to the EPF
scheme will be notified accordingly after approval
from the Ministry
. The proposal
for a corresponding
amendment
in the Income
Tax Act is being taken up with the Ministry of Finance.
Review of minimum balance and waiting period for final PF withdrawal:
Board approved the provisions relating to the minimum balance requirement and waiting period for withdrawal, with a view to safeguarding the long-term social security interests of EPF members. A provision had earlier been made for earmarking 25% of the contributions in the Members’ account as Minimum Balance to be maintained by the member at all times. Now, the minimum balance requirement  for EPF  has been reduced from existing 25% to 10% and waiting period has been reduced from 12 months to 2 months. The changes aim to provide greater financial flexibility to EPF members while safeguarding their long-term social security interests.
Relief in EDLI exemption cases:
The Board approved amendments to EDLI Scheme, 2026, to facilitate resolution of pending legacy exemption cases and provide a six-month window to eligible establishments for renewal of expired exemptions, along with relief from contributions, interest and penal damages for the verified transitional period. This will provide relief to eligible establishments by facilitating the settlement of pending and expired exemption cases, with a six-month window for renewal and relaxation from contributions, interest and penal damages for the verified transitional period.
The proposed amendments aim to resolve long-pending exemption cases under the earlier EDLI Scheme, 1976, and address difficulties faced by establishments during the transition to the new Scheme. This will help establishments that had been maintaining group insurance policies for their employees but could not complete formal exemption or renewal procedures due to administrative and procedural difficulties.
Establishments that maintained continuous group insurance coverage with benefits equal to or better than the statutory EDLI Scheme and duly settled eligible insurance claims may receive relief from contribution liability for the intervening period, along with protection from penal damages and interest, subject to verification. This initiative reflects the Government's commitment to reducing compliance difficulties, ensuring a fair transition to the new legal framework and providing relief to establishments while safeguarding employees' insurance benefits.
Investment in Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs):
The Board in-principle approved to permit investment of up to 3% of fresh accretion in eligible Alternative Investment Funds, within the existing overall investment ceiling, initially through government-backed entities. The decision aims to diversify EPFO's investment portfolio while ensuring prescribed safeguards and investment oversight.
Surrender/cancellation of EPF exemptions
: Proposals concerning surrender of exemption by 27 establishments and cancellation of exemption in four establishments were reviewed. These cases involve transfer of accumulated provident fund savings amounting to approximately ₹5,996 crore to EPFO, covering 1,44,437 members, bringing their accounts under EPFO's direct administration.
Implementation of CITES 2.0:
The Board was apprised of the progress of Centralised IT Enabled System (CITES) 2.0, a centralised, UAN-based digital platform developed by C-DAC to modernise EPFO services. Post implementation of CITIES 2.0 auto-processing of claims increased from 39% to 71% of the total claim processed. The introduction of pre-validation greater automation and simplified withdrawal limits reduced overall rejection ratio from 23% to 7.82%. The overall processing and the average claims settlement time has declined from 11.15 days to 2.57 days.
Budget Estimates 2026-27 and 2027-28 of EPFO:
The Board approved Revised Estimates for 2026-27 and Budget Estimates for 2027-28 of EPFO under EPF, EPS and EDLI Schemes, covering projected receipts, income and expenditure, to ensure effective financial planning and management of EPFO funds.
The proposals placed before the CBT meeting, underline EPFO's commitment to strengthening the country's social security framework, providing greater flexibility in accessing retirement savings, ensuring sustainable pension administration, safeguarding members' investments and delivering technology-driven, transparent and efficient services to EPF members and pensioners.

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Advocates Deeper India-Egypt Cooperation in Digital Governance, Emerging Technologies and Capacity Building
subtitle:
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Interacts with 25 Egyptian Deputy Governors under Special Capacity-Building Programme on Smart Governance

India’s Robust Civil Services Framework and Governance Practices Offer Scope for Mutual Learning Between the Two Nations: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Dr. Jitendra Singh Reaffirms India’s Commitment to Deepening Institutional Cooperation and Tailoring Capacity-Building Programmes to Egypt’s Requirements

Over 1,500 Egyptian Officials Have Benefited from ITEC Programme; India Committed to Expanding Capacity-Building Partnership

content:
India and Egypt can further deepen their longstanding partnership through institutional cooperation, capacity building and mutual exchange of governance practices, with India's experience in digital governance and emerging technologies offering significant opportunities for collaboration, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh said today.
The Minister was interacting with a delegation of 25 Deputy Governors from Egypt participating in the 1st Special Capacity-Building Programme on Smart Governance for Deputy Governors of Egypt, organised by the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG), New Delhi.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India's administrative system has evolved into one of the world's largest and most robust civil services frameworks, often described as the “steel frame of governance”. Given India's diversity and the varying governance requirements across regions, the country has developed a wide range of administrative practices and institutional experiences that can be shared with partner nations. He emphasised that such programmes must encourage mutual learning, with future engagements and training modules shaped around the priorities and requirements of participating countries.
Highlighting the historic relationship between India and Egypt, the Minister said the two nations have shared warm diplomatic ties since the early years of India's Independence, with formal diplomatic relations established shortly thereafter. The partnership has further strengthened in recent years, particularly following the elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's State Visit to Egypt in June 2023, reflecting growing cooperation across economic, political, cultural and strategic areas.
Dr. Jitendra Singh referred to the strong economic engagement between the two countries, with bilateral trade having reached US$ 7.26 billion in FY 2021–22 and standing at US$ 4.8 billion in FY 2024–25. He also highlighted the presence of more than 500 Indian companies registered in Egypt, with investments exceeding US$ 4.5 billion, reflecting the growing depth of commercial and economic cooperation.
The Minister said capacity building remains an important pillar of India-Egypt relations, with more than 1,500 Egyptian officials having benefited from the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme and other Indian training initiatives. He also referred to the Maulana Azad Centre for Indian Culture in Cairo, established in 1992, which promotes cultural exchanges through activities involving Hindi, Urdu, Kathak and Yoga, among others.
Referring to India's governance transformation through technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted the potential for India and Egypt to explore cooperation in Artificial Intelligence, Space Technology, Biotechnology and other emerging areas. He said technological collaboration could contribute to infrastructure development, construction of roads and bridges, housing initiatives and disaster preparedness, while strengthening the capabilities of both countries in an increasingly technology-driven global environment.
Sharing India's citizen-centric governance innovations with the delegation, the Minister explained the functioning of the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS), which records a weekly grievance disposal rate of over 95–97 per cent. He said India's approach combines Artificial Intelligence with human intervention to ensure that grievance redressal remains responsive to citizens' needs, expectations and aspirations.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also discussed the Digital Life Certificate initiative, enabling pensioners to complete life certificate verification through mobile-based face authentication linked to Aadhaar in approximately 40 seconds. He spoke about Mission Karmayogi and its iGOT digital learning platform, which enables role-based capacity building of government officials and promotes a shift towards pragmatic, outcome-oriented public service delivery. He also referred to administrative reforms aimed at reducing file movement time, improving transparency and minimising human interface in recruitment processes.
Responding to the possibilities of adapting Indian governance initiatives in Egypt, the Minister identified India's digital payments ecosystem, particularly UPI and RuPay, as an important area for potential cooperation. He said India's experience in building a large-scale digital transactions ecosystem could offer opportunities for collaboration between the two countries.
Dr. Jitendra Singh reaffirmed India's commitment to further strengthening capacity-building programmes with Egypt and expanding their scope in accordance with the country's specific priorities and requirements. He invited the Egyptian delegation to share their experiences, suggestions and areas of interest, emphasising that sustained interaction and a two-way exchange of knowledge would help develop more meaningful and effective institutional cooperation.
Dr. Surendra Kumar Bagde, Director General, NCGG, welcomed the delegation and described the programme as an important initiative, being the first specialised capacity-building programme organised for senior officials from Egypt. He said the programme was designed to facilitate meaningful interaction on areas of common interest and expressed the Centre's willingness to continue institutional engagement and knowledge exchange with Egypt.
Mr. Ahmed Essameldeen Moussa, Head of the Egyptian Delegation and Deputy Governor of Ismailia Governorate, thanked Dr. Jitendra Singh, the NCGG leadership and the programme team for their support and hospitality. Speaking on behalf of the 25 Deputy Governors, he said the programme reflected the historic friendship and Strategic Partnership between India and Egypt. He referred to the discussions on public infrastructure, anti-corruption strategies, urban local bodies and Mission Karmayogi, along with institutional visits, and expressed confidence that the engagement would serve as a bridge for sustained governance cooperation between the two countries.
The Special Capacity-Building Programme is being held from November 16 to 21, 2026, for representatives from 25 Egyptian Governorates to familiarise them with India's administrative practices, governance innovations, institutional frameworks and public service delivery models. The programme is organised by the National Centre for Good Governance under the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, and sponsored by the Ministry of External Affairs under the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) framework.

subtitle: At the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress in Hyderabad, Minister emphasises innovation, use of alternative materials, scientific planning and accountability in road infrastructure development
date:
